Sports.title: Wafcon 2026 review: Glory for Cameroon, Nigeria flop and Malawi cause a stir
Sports.content:
Cameroon became only the fourth country to lift the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon) title following Nigeria, Equatorial Guinea and South Africa, and only the third to have both a men’s and women’s continental champion, after a 3-0 win over Malawi in Rabat last weekend. The result was significant for several reasons, not least because it gave the competition a new winner after the former champions Nigeria and South Africa were eliminated in the quarter-finals to mark a changing of the guard in the African women’s game.

It is worth remembering that Cameroon did not directly qualify for this edition of the Wafcon and were only added when the tournament was expanded to 16 teams last November. That gave them the opportunity to compete, but almost no one would have picked them as champions based on reputation and results. Cameroon had not reached a Wafcon final in a decade and had never even scored a goal in the final, but had three before half-time against a Malawi side that seemed destined to complete a fairytale.

As debutants and the lowest-ranked team at the event in 153rd place, Malawi scorched their way into the final, in the process confirming a first World Cup appearance in Brazil next year. Malawi and Cameroon will be joined by Morocco and Algeria, who have qualified for the global event for the first time.

Wafcon winners and losers

Two months ago, the former Cameroon goalkeeper Valentine Nguele, who holds a Confederation of African Football (Caf) A coaching licence, was appointed as the national team’s first female coach. She came with a strong record after being part of the support staff at Louves Minproff that won the Cameroonian first division title five times between 2011 and 2020 and was also an assistant coach with FC Ebolowa, who won the title in 2024 and 2026. “Football is a true passion,” she said. “I love the moments I spend on the pitch every day. My style is participative and engaging.”

Under Nguele, Cameroon became a focused and clinical side, which they demonstrated by topping their group. In the quarter-finals they beat the 10-time champions Nigeria, then the hosts, Morocco, in the semi-final and, finally, Malawi. In the process Nguele became the fifth female coach to win Wafcon.

View image in fullscreen Valentine Nguele became the fifth female coach to win the Wafcon title. Photograph: Jalal Morchidi/EPA

By contrast Nigeria failed to make the semi-finals for the first time. Worse was to come as they lost 2-1 to South Africa in their World Cup playoff, meaning they will be absent from the tournament for the first time. The Nigerian Football Federation subsequently sacked Justine Madugu and his entire technical team and announced plans to set up a taskforce to investigate the national team’s failure.

Another team who will be disappointed with their performance at Wafcon are Morocco, who participated in the previous two finals and would have hoped for third time lucky in front of their home fans. They were particularly poor in penalty shootouts, scoring once in four attempts against Cameroon in the semi-finals and twice in five against Algeria in the third-place playoff.

Stars of the tournament

The Cameroon goalkeeper Michaely Bihina won the competition’s golden glove for her ice-cold performances between the posts. Bihina’s standout showings came in the quarter-final, where she made nine saves against Nigeria. In the semi-final, she made three saves in regular time and three more in the penalty shootout to deny Morocco. Bihina kept a clean sheet in the final too, and conceded only two goals in six matches across the tournament.

Wafcon’s best player also came from Cameroon – the midfielder Monique Ngock, whose passion for football stems from watching the Indomitable Lionesses lose the 2016 final. Ngock was 12 years old at the time and remembered sobbing in disappointment. “When I cried in 2016, I said I will take my revenge one day if God gives me that opportunity. I will do everything to bring that trophy,” she said. Ngock very much fulfilled that vow by putting in several excellent performances in Morocco, including in the final, when she kept the dangerous Chawinga sisters in check.

View image in fullscreen Tournament star Monique Ngock of Cameroon reacts after the semi-final win against Morocco. Photograph: Jalal Morchidi/EPA

Temwa Chawinga ultimately took the Golden Boot with five goals – the same number as Barbra Banda (Zambia), Inès Konan (Côte d’Ivoire) and Marie Ngah (Cameroon), who scored two in the final, but Chawinga also had two assists to her name.

Match of the tournament

Tanzania were responsible for the first upset of the tournament when they scored an 87th-minute winner to beat South Africa in the opening match of Group B. The following day Malawi pulled off a heist for the ages when they beat Nigeria 3-2. All the action came in the second half after Temwa Chawinga opened the scoring in the 73rd minute, her sister Tabitha doubling Malawi’s lead six minutes later. Nigeria responded from the spot in added time before Temwa struck again in the 95th minute to give Malawi a 3-1 lead. Nigeria threw everything at their opponents and scored in the 99th minute to set up a thrilling finale but Malawi held firm to begin a rollicking run to the final.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Most improved side

As bronze medallists, Algeria enjoyed their best Wafcon finish and also scored more goals at this tournament than in any previous edition – seven. They also had seven different goalscorers at the tournament, including the impressive 20-year-old Mélissa Bethi, who has been signed by Washington Spirit.

View image in fullscreen The hosts, Morocco, were well supported but other games were often sparsely attended. Photograph: Jalal Morchidi/EPA

Attendances

Stadiums were sparsely populated for most of the tournament, with on-the-ground reports indicating a lack of branding and awareness. Tickets went on sale less than a week before the tournament kicked off, priced between 20 and 50 Moroccan dirhams (£1.59 to £3.98), but such affordability did not have the required impact. This was also the third successive Wafcon held in Morocco, and though official numbers are not in they are unlikely to match the 2022 tournament, where more than 50,000 fans watched the final.

Get in touch

If you have any questions or comments about any of our newsletters please email moving.goalposts@theguardian.com.

Sports.title: ‘He doubted’: Mourinho says Real Madrid didn’t want Rodri after hesitation over move
Sports.content:
José Mourinho has confirmed Real Madrid made Rodri an offer and that he spoke to him about joining the club, but claimed the player’s doubts about the transfer made him unsure about signing Spain’s World Cup-winning captain.

On the same day Rodri was presented at Barcelona following the completion of a €75m (£65.4m) move from Manchester City that the midfielder said was “always my first choice”, Mourinho insisted he would not miss the him at the Santiago Bernabéu. “I spoke to him a couple of times and Real Madrid made him a very good offer,” Mourinho said in an interview with El Chiringuito.

“Without negotiating with City, the club were in contact with Rodri and made him an important offer. Rodrigo had doubts, he doubted. And his doubts created doubts in me. He is an extraordinary player and he behaved in the right way with us. I have nothing bad to say. But Real Madrid are so big that you can’t have players who have to think twice. You get in touch with a player and the player says: ‘When do I go?’ That’s how it works.”

Rodri had three offers to leave City after the World Cup, from Paris Saint-Germain, Real and Barcelona. Having ruled out PSG because he wanted to return to Spain, the 30-year-old eventually chose Barcelona, where he will join eight of his international teammates. When it was put to Mourinho that the move could be seen as a victory for Barcelona over their great rivals, he replied: “Victories are on the pitch, trophies”.

Real have not signed an alternative midfielder, despite their pursuit of Rodri and that being a clear hole in a team that has failed to win a major trophy in the past two seasons. Mourinho feels sure, however, that he does not need to bring in any further players. “I am not saying that there will not be any more signings because the market is still open, but if you ask me directly whether the squad is complete, for me yes it is,” said the 63-year-old ahead of his second stint managing in Madrid. “It’s complete, closed. I like [my squad] a lot.

“I don’t miss Rodrigo. We have solutions, we have quality, we have players who maybe you look at and you judge them on what they have done [before] but I like to think that I have the ability to improve players. A player that is one thing today can be a different player tomorrow.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa expect another bid from Al-Hilal for Ollie Watkins
Sports.content:
Aston Villa are braced for another bid from Al-Hilal for Ollie Watkins, after rejecting an offer worth almost £40m for the striker. Al-Hilal are pursuing a move for Villa’s all-time Premier League goalscorer, who has reached double figures in the top flight in his six seasons at the club after joining from Brentford.

If Villa sell Watkins, who has two years remaining on his contract, they would seek to replace the 30-year-old England striker and Unai Emery is a big admirer of Nicolas Jackson, but Chelsea’s valuation of £65m is thought to be prohibitive to any deal. There is an acceptance at Villa that any marquee arrival before the close of the window would probably have to follow another major sale, owing to Premier League’s financial regulations.

Emery has had to significantly reshape his squad this summer after the departures of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, who joined Chelsea, Manchester United and Paris Saint-Germain respectively. Rogers left in a deal worth £117m to become the most expensive British player.

Villa have signed Zion Suzuki as a replacement for Emiliano Martínez, whose future remains unclear. Suzuki, a £30m buy from Parma, will be the first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Premier League.

Villa have completed the £17m signing of Matteo Ruggeri from Atlético Madrid and remain in talks with Bayern Munich over a deal for João Palhinha and West Ham for Aaron Wan-Bissaka. Villa have also signed Johan Manzambi from Freiburg for a club-record £52m and Joao Gomes from Wolves for £38m.

There could be further sales, with Villa hoping to find Martínez a new club, while Arsenal remain interested in signing the England defender Ezri Konsa.

Villa gave Watkins, together with Martínez and Konsa, an extended four-week break after the World Cup. Emery said Watkins volunteered to play in last week’s Super Cup, but the manager advised him to continue to rest.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 15: Manchester City
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 2nd (NB: this is not necessarily Jamie Jackson’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 2nd

Prospects

Enzo Maresca was already in herculean task mode by signing on as the man charged with continuing the dynasty built by Pep Guardiola at Manchester City before Rodri decided to leave the club and join Barcelona. The 30-year-old may be headed for a second Ballon d’Or after his displays in Spain’s triumphant World Cup campaign, so the loss of a midfielder capable of moulding games domestically and in the Champions League represents a sizeable blow for Maresca.

There are further negatives too, with John Stones, Nathan Aké and Bernardo Silva also no longer at City. On the positive side, Elliot Anderson has joined for £116m from Nottingham Forest having impressed for England at the World Cup. City’s new manager also has Erling Haaland, who will be favourite to claim a fourth Premier League Golden Boot in five seasons. Less certain is how Phil Foden will perform despite being boosted by a bumper new contract. Can the boy from Stockport dovetail with Rayan Cherki and once more pull the strings for his boyhood side?

Off-field picture

City are a best-in-class organisation, who can be used as an exemplar of how to pursue excellence on and off the field. This, of course, would change were they found guilty over the 130 charges brought against them for alleged breaches of Premier League rules. It has been more than three years since the charges were announced, with City continuing to deny any wrongdoing. The new Pep Guardiola Stand, opened for the great man’s final home game last season, means 61,000 fans can now witness Haaland and co go to work, the Etihad Stadium’s capacity having previously stood at 53,400.

Owner-fan relationship

Sheikh Mansour is a hero to the City faithful for a glittering period of ownership that has elevated their team to a domestic and continental superpower. Listening to fans, the club have also frozen ticket prices for a third consecutive season. Meanwhile in the Pep Guardiola Stand, 4,000 new flexi season tickets – a pay-as-you-go scheme – have sold out, half of which are for junior fans, with City introducing £10 seats for those who live in the five wards around the ground.

The manager

Is Maresca courageous for following The Man or naive for believing he can? Over to the 46-year-old, who has zero doubt the City job is no chalice laced with poison. “It’s fantastic, nice and exciting, and for me, a privilege,” he said. “First of all, the most important thing has been that Khaldoon [al-Mubarak, the chair], Hugo [Viana, the director of football] and Ferran [Soriano, the chief executive] all speak the same language in terms of this is a club that has to win games, titles and has to compete, but we also talk about how we can continue to make this club better, season after season.” Maresca’s CV shows the Championship crown with Leicester, and the Conference League and Club World Cup glory with Chelsea. How he would love to add the Premier League title to that roll of honour at the first time of asking.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Elliot Anderson of Manchester City holds off Martin Ødegaard and Myles Lewis-Skelly of Arsenal during the 2026 FA Community Shield. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images

Rodri’s departure offers Anderson an opportunity to run City’s midfield. Can he do so? Maresca and Viana obviously believe this or £116m would not have been splurged on the lad from Whitley Bay who could not nail down a starting berth for Newcastle in five years as a senior professional there. At the World Cup there were flashes of a schemer who can spray passes long range – Rodri-style – as well as the shorter, metronomic stuff. What’s for sure is that Anderson has a career-defining opportunity in front of him.

Stat attack

Manchester City conceded more league goals from set pieces last season than they had in the previous two campaigns combined. They were costly at times too: the winning goals in their losses at Aston Villa and Newcastle both came from corners, for instance. Maresca’s Chelsea conceded from a set play every three league games so his record there was a shade worse than City’s in 2025-26. He has work to do.

Set for a breakthrough

Vitor Reis was signed in January 2025 and made four appearances that season. The defender’s debut was also forgettable as, then 19, he was hooked at half-time with City trailing 1-0 at Leyton Orient in the FA Cup fourth round. The Brazilian played all of the 3-1 victory in the following round, and was fielded in the 89th-minute of the 2-0 league victory at Leicester in April before his sole other City appearance: a full outing in the 2-0 Club World Cup win over Wydad Casablanca that June. Last season’s loan at City’s sister club Girona ended in relegation, but Reis is said to have impressed.

World Cup impact

The departed Rodri made real the ultimate fantasy of all players by captaining his country to the World Cup and being so vital to that glory that he was named player of the tournament. Cherki fared less well, making six substitute appearances and one start for a France side that fell, to Spain, in the semi-finals. France’s attacking ranks may overflow with quality, but for a player with magic in both boots, that seemed odd.

Sports.title: Is Turkey home to savvy signings or a new retirement league? We’ll soon find out
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah plays in Turkey now. So do Romelu Lukaku and Leandro Trossard and Leroy Sané and Nathan Aké. Mason Greenwood and N’Golo Kanté and Dusan Vlahovic, too.

Bruno Fernandes and Gabriel Martinelli may yet follow them there, depending on negotiations and moods and whatever else compels a footballer to leave one club for another.

Victor Osimhen, one of the world’s highest-rated strikers, was already at Galatasaray, where he has hammered in 43 league goals in two seasons, plus this campaign’s opener.

Salah, the Super Lig’s signature signing, will reportedly earn about as much at Trabzonspor as he did with Liverpool last season, where he was one of the Premier League’s highest earners – on account of the net salary structure in Turkey.

As the Saudi Pro League, which flooded the game with billions in cash when it lured Cristiano Ronaldo and Neymar in 2023, scales back its ambitions, the Turkish league has stepped into the void. A flurry of investment by its four biggest clubs – Galatasaray, Fenerbahce, Besiktas and Trabzonspor – is remaking it into the new moneyed destination league for the game’s ageing and the underplayed and the overpaid and the overvalued. Or perhaps they’ve made a series of savvy signings; we’ll soon find out.

Unlike in previous spending sprees by leagues seeking to claim a more prominent spot in the transfer market ecosystem, the Super Lig doesn’t seem to have benefited from massive investment from a soft-power nation-building project or the sudden interest of oligarchs. Rather – and it’s all slightly confounding – it appears to have more to do with the collapse of the Turkish lira relative to the euro, which went from trading at €0.10 half a decade ago to about €0.018 today. While their clubs pay their players in lira, revenue from European competition and foreign broadcasts is paid out in euros. The long and short of it is that the big four Turkish clubs can now afford players they previously couldn’t because they can write down more of their earnings on their balance sheets.

As such, Turkey joins an increasingly long line of unconventional homes for some of the game’s biggest names. Every few years, some new league invests heavily in hopes of finding a shortcut into the firmament of the world’s best-regarded competitions. Before Saudi Arabia, it was China, where it was the stated objective of President Xi Jinping and his government to leverage the sport as “a must to build China into a sports powerhouse as part of the Chinese dream”. Eventually, Chinese soccer awoke from that dream with a start.

Before that, it was the Russian Premier League, when sanctioned oil billionaire Suleyman Kerimov bought Anzhi Makhachkala and plowed in hundreds of millions to lure some of the world’s top players. That set off an arms race with Zenit St Petersburg, Rubin Kazan and Dynamo Moscow, before the spending fever broke just a few years later when Kerimov backed off.

The Brazilian league has had flurries of pricey signings over the years – although mostly focused on bringing home the country’s wayward sons – in apparent accordance with the state of the nation’s economy and bank balances. In January, Flamengo brought Lucas Paquetá back from West Ham for an astounding $50m, setting a new Brazilian record for an incoming transfer, dwarfing the $32m Cruzeiro had paid Zenit for Gerson just 20 days earlier.

During its Beckham Era, Major League Soccer was routinely paying above-market rates to lure Thierry Henry, Robbie Keane and the like. And before that, the Qatar Stars League tried to deliver on its name by drawing Gabriel Batistuta, Pep Guardiola, Frank de Boer, Marcel Desailly and others for a final payday.

Every one of these leagues moved on from this gambit before long, switching to some other strategy, or however they spun the decision to cap the money gusher.

It should probably be pointed out here that unlike most of the aforementioned circuits, Turkey actually has a thriving and long-established football and fan culture. That makes it feel slightly different this time around, as Turkish clubs have earned credibility as the homes of star players, unexpected though their arrivals may be, and because those players will probably still appear in the Champions League (Galatasaray qualified automatically; Fenerbahce are in the qualifiers) and Europa League (Trabzonspor and Besiktas are both in the qualifying rounds).

All the same, the Turkish clubs now take the mantle of acting as a kind of bailout fund for Europe’s storied leagues, where clubs from the latter can offload their distressed assets. At a minimum, these nouveaux riche leagues provide a hefty cash injection to the old-money center of the European game.

In the end, nothing much ever comes of this play for the newly ambitious. They move on, eventually. The whole thing turns out to be counterproductive. Because rather than match the status of the legacy competitions they hope to challenge, they wind up bankrolling them, cementing the chasm between them.

They learn that lesson before long and the money dries up. But no matter, there is always some fresh source of dumb money out there.

Sports.title: March, May and more: footballers scoring in months that match their names | The Knowledge
Sports.content:
“Birmingham’s August Priske scored the only goal at Swansea in the League Cup on 8 August. Can you think of any other examples of players scoring in their namesake months?” wonders Paul Tiffen.

Our wonderful readers have managed to cover the entire year, pretty much, so let’s get going. The list below includes just some of the many examples you sent in.

January

“Not all last names exist for English months, so I also took month names in some other languages,” writes Mykola Kozlenko. “I only accepted exact spellings, [so] I don’t accept Auguste or Augustin for the month of August, but Agosto is fine.” As is Janvier, which gave Mykola their first goalscorer: “Nicolas Janvier. Scored on 30 January 2016 for Lannion v Rennes Reserves.”

February

“Jayden Fevrier. Scored on 3 February 2024 for Colchester against Forest Green Rovers,” writes Mykola.

March

“In German, March is ‘März’,” writes Dirk Maas. “In the 1992-93 edition of the 2. Bundesliga, Heiko März scored twice in March, for Hansa Rostock against St. Pauli and Darmstadt.” Dirk also points out that Solly March’s portfolio of goals in March includes two for Brighton in FA Cup quarter-finals: against Millwall in 2019 and Grimsby in 2023.

View image in fullscreen Solly March heads home for Brighton in their 5-0 FA Cup quarter-final victory over Grimsby in March 2023. Photograph: Andrew Matthews/PA

April

“April Heinrichs scored twice for the USA on April Fools’ Day 1991 against Yugoslavia in the Grand Hotel Varna Tournament in Bulgaria,” writes Dan Almond. “She also scored on 3 April against Hungary and again in the final as the USA beat USSR 5-0.”

May

“David May scored the opening goal in Manchester United’s final game of the 1995-96 season,” writes Sinan Eccles. “The 3-0 win against Middlesbrough at the Riverside on 5 May 1996 secured the title for United. Andy Cole and Ryan Giggs scored the others. Eric Cantona got the late winner in a 1-0 victory over Liverpool in the FA Cup final to secure United their second domestic double in three seasons.”

View image in fullscreen David May (right) is congratulated by Roy Keane after opening the scoring against Middlesbrough in May 1996. Photograph: Michael Mayhew/Allstar

Matt Beaumont points out that Alfie May scored on 7 May 2023 for Cheltenham Town v Charlton – and then joined the Addicks two months later, leaving as Cheltenham’s record goalscorer.

June

Back to Mykola Kozlenko: “Brazil’s Edigar Junio scored on 22 June 2019 for Yokohama F Marinos against Matsumoto Yamaga in the J-League.”

View image in fullscreen Edigar Junio scores the winner for Yokohama F Marinos in their J-League match against Matsumoto Yamaga in June 2019. Photograph: Masashi Hara/Getty Images

July

Three goalscoring Julios in July were found by Mykola …

Anderson Julio (Ecuador), 13 July 2023, Real Salt Lake v Sporting KC

Jhojan Julio (Ecuador), 31 July 2019, LDU Quito v Olimpia

Junior Julio Bueno (Armenia), 20 July 2023, Ararat-Armenia v Egnatia

View image in fullscreen Anderson Julio wheels away in celebration after scoring for Real Salt Lake at Sporting Kansas City in July 2023. Photograph: Bill Barrett/ISI Photos/Getty Images

August

Michael St John-Mcalister offers August Lohapresert, the Sweden-born midfielder who won an under-23 cap for Thailand. Turns out the internet isn’t entirely bad, for it has provided details of Gais Under-19’s 2-1 victory over Kalmar FF Under-19s on 16 August 2012. Both Gais’s goals were scored by their substitute, the aforementioned Lohapresert.

September

Back to Mykola for the last few. “Mateusz Wrzesien (Poland). Scored on 26 September 2018 for Baltyk Koszalin v Rozwoj Katowice.” We should probably clarify that Wrzesien is September in Polish.

October

Pasquale Ottobre scored a brace on 25 October 2009 for Fidelis Andros against Virtus Lanciano in Italy’s Lega Pro. (Note: Pasquale is a name usually given to those born around Easter or Passover, although Ottobre was born in … November.)

November

Tymofiy Lystopad (Ukraine). Scored on 7 November 2015 in Desna Chernihiv v Naftovyk-Ukrnafta Okhtyrka. Lystopad is November in Ukrainian

December

This was the only month for which we didn’t receive a goalscoring answer, but Mykola Kozlenko did find a manager: Frantz Décembre, the Haitian who managed several clubs in the 2010s. We don’t have a specific game, but it’s probably a fair bet that at least one of his teams scored at least one goal in December.

Caught in no-man’s land

“In the recent Leagues Cup clash between Tigres and Vancouver Whitecaps, Tigres goalkeeper Nahuel Guzmán received a straight red card for pushing the referee. The incident took place near the halfway line. What is the furthest upfield that a goalkeeper has received a straight red card?” asks Eoin Fegan.

Back in 2015, West Ham’s Adrián came forward for a corner late on against Leicester at Upton Park – but when the ball was cleared and the visitors threatened to break, the keeper caught Jamie Vardy with a high boot, and was shown a straight red card. Adrián insisted that the foul was accidental, tweeting: “Never in my career I have kicked nobody with bad intention to deserve a red card.” West Ham appealed the decision, but it was upheld and Adrián received a three-match ban.

Knowledge archive

In the Highland League match on 8 August between Forres Mechanics and Fraserburgh, Forres defender Ewan Neil was sent off for a foul just seven seconds after the match kicked off, and Fraserburgh awarded a penalty kick,” writes Sid Bright. “What is the quickest penalty ever awarded in a match?”

We previously looked at this topic in 2017, after a similar question from Stephen Yoxall. He saw his team, Witton Albion, win a penalty after six seconds in an FA Trophy tie against Chester FC when Tolani Omotola was fouled by Blaine Hudson.

Here’s what we wrote at the time: “Witton’s penalty was awarded after just 6.18 seconds. It was saved, but Bradley Bauress followed up his own spot-kick to score the rebound. Omotola was then sent off later in the first half, before Hudson – probably fortunate to avoid a dismissal with the initial penalty – picked up a second booking during the second period. Witton’s coach Paul Moore was later sent to the stands, before the visitors’ Matthew Devine gave away a late penalty, which earned him a red card, and Chester an equaliser. The nine men were beaten when Chester’s Elliott Durrell grabbed an injury-time winner.”

We found a number of other early examples, but nothing to beat 6.18 seconds – we even had a word with the people behind the Guinness Book of World Records. Forres Mechanics went close with their recent effort, but we have found a quicker penalty, awarded to Tanzania in a World Cup qualifier against Madagascar in September 2021.

As reported by the BBC, Tanzania launched it long from kick off, and Simon Msuva was brought down on the edge of the area by Madagascar keeper Melvin Adrien. The foul was committed after just four seconds, with the spot-kick given a second later. Erasto Nyoni stepped up to convert it, setting the hosts up for a 3-2 victory.

Are there any faster penalties we’ve missed? Get in touch …

Can you help?

“Marquinhos won his 40th trophy in club football when Paris Saint-Germain beat Aston Villa in the Super Cup,” notes Paul Gage. “Has any player won more?”

View image in fullscreen Another one for the collection: Marquinhos with the Uefa Super Cup. Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images

“The last full-time England manager to have won the English top flight as a coach was Don Revie (1974-77). Does any country have a longer drought?” asks Albert from Vienna.

“Midnite are the 26-27 shirt sponsors for three Championship sides; Middlesbrough, Sheffield United and Wolves,” notes Peter Skilton. “This means they will be the sponsors of at least one of the teams in 24% of Championship fixtures this season. “Is this a record, and which brand has sponsored the most different teams in a single league?”

“On 11 July 2010, Maarten Stekelenburg and Gregory van der Wiel played in the World Cup final against Spain,” begins Dirk Maas. “Seventeen days later came their next match, for Ajax against PAOK in the Champions League qualifiers. Have any other European players played their next competitive game so soon after a World Cup final?

“Arsenal Tivat have truly embodied the boring, boring Arsenal stereotype by starting the Montenegrin league season with three successive 0-0 draws. Has any side ever managed to start a season in a less entertaining manner than this?” asks Richard Wilson.

“When watching the new Mourinho documentary on Netflix, there was some footage of old Portuguese football – I think it was Vitória Setubal or Belenenses – and the goalmouth had a weird sand triangle within the six-yard box. The triangle started at each post and ended in the middle of the six-yard box. It looked like a baseball field. I’ve never seen this before. Was it commonplace in Portugal or anywhere else?” asks Chris Ward.

“Xavi Simons was named after Xavi Hernández, who will be his coach at international level after taking the Netherlands job,” notes Niall McVeigh. “Are there any other examples of footballers playing for coaches they are named after (but not related to)?”

“Has a club’s player-manager ever been called up for an international cap, or travelled to play during an international break in the club season?” asks Frederick Sondheimer-Acosta.

Sports.title: Arsenal closing on agreement for Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa
Sports.content:
Arsenal and Aston Villa are closing on an agreement for Ezri Konsa. Daily Mail Sport revealed last week that Arsenal had improved their offer to £40m plus add ons and talks were ongoing as they try to reach a compromise. Villa have been pushing for closer to £60m for the England centre-back. Arsenal enquired about Bayer Leverkusen's Jarell Quansah as an alternative option. Konsa, 28, has made 286 appearances for Aston Villa since joining the club in 2019 from Brentford. The defender featured in 48 matches last season as Aston Villa won the Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. Arsenal and Aston Villa are closing on agreement for England international Ezri Konsa

Your browser does not support iframes.

Konsa had served as Aston Villa’s vice captain last season, wearing the armband when John McGinn was absent. The defender had been a vital player for England throughout the World Cup. Konsa started seven of the Three Lions' eight matches at the tournament, with Thomas Tuchel largely partnering him with Marc Guehi at the heart of the defence. He also filled in at right back during England's quarter-final victory over Norway.

Sports.title: Revealed: How neurologists 'signed off' on Bayern star Jamal Musiala playing again between two terrifying on-pitch collapses in just four days - and he could return this weekend
Sports.content:
Revealed: How neurologists 'signed off' on Bayern star Jamal Musiala playing again between two terrifying on-pitch collapses in just four days - and he could return this weekend

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Bayern Munich honorary president Uli Hoeness has revealed neurologists provided written confirmation Jamal Musiala was able to play after admitting he was left 'speechless' by the star collapsing twice on the pitch in four days.

Musiala, 23, revealed on Tuesday that he is receiving treatment for a 'neurological dysfunction', which has led to his on pitch collapses.

The Bayern star fell just six minutes after coming off the bench during their 4-2 victory over Heidenheim in a pre-season friendly.

Harry Kane was one of the first to react to the situation, gesturing to his team-mates to form a shield around Musiala for his privacy. While some had already headed over to form a barrier, the 33-year-old was seen waving his arm to get more players to join them.

The German attacker received medical treatment after the incident, but appeared to be dazed and had to be supported as he walked off the pitch, with Cassiano Kiala coming on in his place in the 61st minute.

Musiala also collapsed during Bayern's 3-1 friendly victory over RB Leipzig in the sweltering heat on Saturday.

Jamal Musiala was helped off the pitch on Tuesday after collapsing for the second time in four days

Musiala's team-mates had surrounded him to protect his privacy, with the attacker later revealing that he has been suffering from a 'neurological dysfunction' leading to the collapses

Bayern honoary president Uli Hoeness has explained the club were given written confirmation from neurologists that Musiala could play and admitted they were aware of his condition

Footage showed Musiala looking disorientated while waiting for the match to restart after he had scored, with Ismael Saibari sprinting over to catch him before he hit the ground.

In a statement, Musiala disclosed he has been 'diagnosed with brief, temporary - but treatable - absence seizures resulting from a neurological dysfunction'.

Hoeness, speaking to Sky and RTL on Wednesday, confirmed an agreement had been reached after the first incident that Musiala would go public with his condition if he suffered another collapse.

The Bayern honorary president confirmed the club had been aware of Musiala's condition and had sought confirmation from neurologists that the attacker was able to play.

'We've been aware of the problems for some time now. Against Leipzig, it happened for the first time on the pitch, and it was visible to everyone,' Hoeness said.

'At that point, we thought, 'If it doesn't happen again so quickly, then the medication he's taking will help.' But when it happened again four days later, in the same way, it completely floored me.

'I was speechless, which is rare for me. We were expecting everything but this recurrence of these problems. It's a tragedy, especially for Jamal.'

He added: 'We've already taken some precautions. The treating physicians, the neurologists, gave us written confirmation, because it was absolutely essential for us that, from their perspective, there were no concerns about Jamal participating in high-performance sports.

Musiala had collapsed on Saturday, leading to the player and club agreeing he would go public with his condition if a similar event occurred

Hoeness added that Bayern Munich have offered Musiala their 'unconditional support' and were looking to find a way to deal with his situation

'Without that, we would have been acting negligently. Since we received this written confirmation, we've been sleeping a bit more soundly. But to be honest, I'm speechless and without a real solution.'

Hoeness added that Bayern Munich have offered Musiala their 'unconditional support' and were looking to find a way to deal with his situation.

'There have been occasional indications and one or two problems, but these never occurred within our club.

'I don't know if it ever happened in training. Our people rightly keep that confidential. But now, with these two incidents, it is of course a problem. Primarily for Jamal as a person.

'I go to bed thinking about him and wake up thinking about him. But of course, in the medium term, it's also a problem for the club, because we are pretty much speechless at the moment.

'We couldn't have prepared for this, and we first have to learn how to deal with this situation.'

Musiala had provided a full update to fans about his condition on Tuesday night by sharing an update on Instagram.

He said: 'First things first, I am doing well. I am incredibly grateful for your messages and your support!

Musiala stated on Tuesday that there is 'no further health risk involved' and it was his 'personal wish to face this challenge; with the medical clearance of the neurologists'

'I understand that many of you are worried. I would like to put those concerns to rest today and explain the situation: I have been diagnosed with brief, temporary - but treatable - absence seizures resulting from a neurological dysfunction.

'These can lead to the kind of incidents seen recently, such as during the match against Leipzig or the game in Heidenheim.

'I know they might look alarming at first glance, but for me, they are currently part of my everyday life. I am receiving excellent medical care and remain very optimistic. FC Bayern and my personal support network are right by my side, helping me through this.'

Musiala went on to insist that he remained in good spirits and added that he was not putting himself in danger by continuing to play.

'Importantly, there is no further health risk involved,' Musiala added. 'In close consultation and regular contact with the experts, it was my personal wish to face this challenge; with the medical clearance of the neurologists, I want to continue doing what helps my recovery most: simply living my life and pursuing my passion for playing football.

'I have taken full responsibility for this decision. Overall, I feel very positive and am on the right track.

'What helps me most on this journey is continuing to chase victories and titles with my team and with your amazing support.

'I hope this helps you understand the situation better. At the same time, I ask for your understanding regarding my wish to keep this matter private, sharing it only with my closest circle, the club, and the medical experts.'

Sports.title: Aston Villa braced for fourth Ollie Watkins bid from Saudi side, with player open to switch - as Newcastle offered former Chelsea forward Christopher Nkunku: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... Villa braced for another Watkins bid Aston Villa anticipate a fourth bid from Al Hilal for striker Ollie Watkins. The England international is open to the move but so far Villa have rejected their advances and want to keep the 30-year-old. Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins is understood to be open to a move to Saudi Arabia The latest bid of £38m was rejected on Tuesday evening. Villa maintain interested in Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson and have confirmed the signings of Matteo Ruggeri and Zion Suzuki. Left back Ruggeri, 24, joins from Atletico Madrid, while goalkeeper Suzuki, 23, arrives after two years in Italy with Parma. Meanwhile, Rangers have signed right back Kosta Nedeljkovic from Villa. The 20-year-old has moved to Ibrox on a season-long loan, with a £4m obligation to buy, which will be triggered by the number of games he plays. As Daily Mail Sport revealed last week, Villa are signing Aaron Wan Bissaka on loan from West Ham pending his medical today. The deal can become an obligation to buy at around £18million. Jones keen on Inter switch Inter Milan have held further talks with Liverpool today over the transfer of Curtis Jones. The Italians are confident of finding agreement around a £30million fee for the midfielder. Jones would link up with John Stones and Djed Spence at Inter if all goes to plan. Jones has been eager to start more regularly and is ready for a fresh challenge. Inter have been pursuing 25-year-old Jones since December. Toon's Nkunku offer Newcastle have been offered the chance to sign former Chelsea forward Christopher Nkunku from AC Milan. However, their priority remains to sign a midfielder first hence talks with Man City for Nico Gonzalez. Other targets are also being discussed. Nkunku has been told he can leave Milan and has interest from RB Leipzig among others. Toon are also closing on Genclerbirligi’s midfielder Ousmane Diabate. The highly-rated 18-year-old had been set for Brentford while Tottenham had also shown interest. However, Newcastle look to have won the race with the teenager likely to stay on loan in Turkey for another season. Diabate, a defensive midfielder, has played 10 matches for the U19s and seven for Genclerbirligi’s first team so far. Liverpool defensive prospect in talks over La Liga move Liverpool defensive prospect Ifeanyi Ndukwe is in talks to join Levante on loan. The 18-year-old does not qualify for a work permit in England so is having to be loaned out. The Austrian youth international has excelled during Liverpool's pre-season and the club have high hopes for his future. First team football in a top league such as La Liga is viewed as an integral next step. He also has interest from Portugal and Germany. Winger Kieran Morrison is joining Sheffield Wednesday on loan today. Liverpool continue to discuss a move for Bradley Barcola at Paris St Germain but a deal for his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye is unlikely Konsa nearing Arsenal move... Arsenal and Aston Villa are closing on agreement for Ezri Konsa. Daily Mail Sport revealed last week that Arsenal had improved their offer to £40m plus add ons and talks were ongoing as they try to reach a compromise. Read the full story here. As Gunners move for United youngster Arsenal are also working on a deal for 20-year-old right back Habeeb Ogunneye from Manchester United. Arsenal want players to boost their U21s squad and have also shown interest in United's James Scanlon. Gibraltar international winger Scanlon was on loan at Swindon Town last season. England youth international Ogunneye had a spell at Newport on loan. Baleba close to United switch Manchester United are closing on a £65million deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba. Talks resumed for the Cameroon international in recent weeks after it became apparent his ankle ligament injury was not as serious as first feared. Read the full story here. Pogba tears up Monaco deal Monaco have confirmed that Paul Pogba has left by mutual agreement, bringing his time at the Ligue 1 club to a premature end. The 33-year-old former Manchester United midfielder is now a free agent and has been offered to clubs in the MLS. Read the full story here. Paul Pogba's time at Monaco is over - with MLS clubs now considering a move for the former Man United midfielder Farke reunites with Elvedi Leeds have signed Nico Elvedi from Borussia Monchengladbach. The final fee is £6.5m rising to £8.5m with bonuses. The 29-year-old Switzerland international centre back worked with Daniel Farke previously at the Bundesliga club. James set for Wolves move Rennes midfielder Jordan James is poised to finalise his move to Wolves today pending his medical. The Wales international midfielder is joining on an initial loan deal with an option to sign permanently for around £10m. He impressed on loan at Leicester last season scoring 11 goals in 34 games and had interest from Middlesbrough and West Ham. Chelsea defender closes on Italy move Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has arrived at Villa Stuart in Rome ahead of his medical this morning. The 25-year-old centre back is joining Napoli on loan for around £2.5m with an option for the deal to become permanent at £23m. Mamadou Sarr, meanwhile, is emerging as a target for Real Sociedad and Al Hilal. The 20-year-old has been expected to go on loan in the Premier League and interest there remains. The Senegal international was recalled from a loan at Strasbourg to provide cover last season and started in their FA Cup win over Hull. Piroe party at West Ham West Ham have signed Joel Piroe on loan from Leeds until the end of the season. The deal also includes an option for it to become permanent, which will be activated should certain conditions be met, including West Ham winning promotion back to the Premier League. Joel Piroe has joined West Ham on loan from Leeds West Ham turned to 27-year-old Piroe after hitting an impasse in talks for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott who is joining Real Betis for £17m plus add ons. Piroe, who has scored 73 goals in the Championship during spells with Leeds and Swansea , said: 'I see West Ham as a Club that really wants to be in the Premier League, and I think should be in the Premier League. 'With my experience, I think I can help the Club a lot to achieve what they want to achieve, and I think it’s a good opportunity for me to show what I’ve learnt and how I’ve grown as a football player over the years.' Piroe finished the 2024-25 season as the Championship's top scorer, helping Leeds United earn promotion to the Premier League. The Hammers remain an option for free agent Jamie Vardy. Potters snare Ipswich pair Stoke have agreed a fee of around £6million with Ipswich for striker George Hirst and are also taking Ipswich full back Ben Johnson on loan. Scotland international Hirst is to undergo medical later today. The fee will increase on performance related bonuses. Sports.title: Curtis Jones to leave Liverpool in £30m transfer to Inter Milan - as the third member of Italian giants' English revolution this summer
Sports.content:
Inter Milan are on the verge of signing Liverpool midfielder Curtis Jones after a summer-long back and forth.

The six-time England international, who joined Liverpool aged nine, has had his heart set on a move to Serie A for some time after failing to regularly establish himself as a starter at Anfield.

And it now appears he will leave, with the two clubs in dialogue. A fee of around £30million will get the deal done, with Inter signaling they are ready to pay it.

The Italian champions had a bid of around £21m turned down earlier in the summer and, if they sign Jones, he will be the third Englishman they have bought this window after Manchester City's John Stones and Tottenham's Djed Spence.

Liverpool meanwhile are preparing for their first season under new manager Andoni Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot following the Dutchman's dismissal at the end of last season.

The six-time England international, who joined Liverpool aged nine, has had his heart set on a move to Serie A for some time after failing to regularly establish himself as a starter at Anfield

It appears Jones will follow Tottenham's Djed Spence as an Englishman heading to Inter

John Stones also moved to the San Siro on a free transfer from Manchester City this summer

The Italian press expect an official announcement on Jones to follow within 'hours' and say a medical has already been scheduled for him.

After spending over £450million on new signings including Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer, the 2024-25 Premier League champions struggled to reach the same heights again under the Dutchman and only narrowly managed to qualify for the Champions League with a fifth-place finish last term.

Liverpool, who waved farewell to Mohamed Salah, Andrew Robertson and Ibrahima Konate at the start of the summer, have so far recruited centre-half Jeremy Jacquet from Stade Rennais and left winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna ahead of the new campaign.

While theoretically all first-team places are up for grabs under new boss Iraola, Jones has been viewed as a squad player at the club in recent seasons, playing second fiddle to fellow central midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister, Ryan Gravenberch and Wirtz under Slot and previously Jurgen Klopp.

Sports.title: Man United close in on £65m deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba
Sports.content:
Man United close in on £65m deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United are closing in on a £65million deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba.

Talks resumed for the 22-year-old Cameroon international in recent weeks after it became clear the ankle ligament injury he suffered during a pre-season friendly against Strasbourg in early August was not as serious as initially feared.

Baleba is expected to return to fitness towards the end of September and is understood to be poised to sign a five-year contract at Old Trafford, keeping him at the club until 2031.

Baleba has been a target for Manchester United for the past year after impressing initially with his industrious performances at Brighton, but he was valued around £75m.

His form dropped away in the second half of last season but United still see enough potential to invest in with his age.

Baleba has also drawn enquiries from Newcastle United in recent weeks.

Talks resumed for the 22-year-old after it became clear the ankle ligament injury he suffered during a pre-season friendly in early August was not as serious as initially feared

With plans to invest in three central midfielders, United have already completed two major signings in Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa (£35m), and Andrey Santo from Chelsea (£50m)

Baleba joined Brighton from Lille for just £23m in 2023 and immediately impressed, establishing himself as one of the most exciting young midfielders in the top-flight.

His dynamism and ability to break the press made him a key figure in Roberto De Zerbi's side before Fabian Hurzeler took charge in 2024.

United looked to sign Baleba last summer, but Brighton wanted in excess of £100m for him and stood firm.

Speaking in October, Brighton's chairman Tony Bloom said: 'There was interest from Manchester United, and we said that he wasn't available this summer and they went away.

'His improvement has been immense. He's a massively important player to this football club, and we're just delighted that he's with us for this season.'

Last season Hurzeler said that the player had struggled with the speculation of a move to United.

'I think it's normal for a young player when the media creates the noise around him,' the young manager said. 'It's not easy for this player to handle it.

'Therefore, we need to give him the time and support so he comes back to his best performance.

'But he's a young player and I think that's something we have to accept, that young players don't always have the face we want to see.'

Prior to Tielemans and Santos' arrival, 21-year-old Kobbie Mainoo was the only established senior central midfielder in the squad

Manuel Ugarte, who United were prepared to offload, sustained a serious knee injury during the World Cup for Uruguay, and will now remain at the club until his expected return in 2027

United set about to reshape their midfield this summer following the departure of the influential Casemiro to MLS side Inter Miami. Manuel Ugarte, who they were prepared to offload, sustained a serious knee injury during the World Cup for Uruguay, will now remain at the club until his expected return at the start of next year.

With plans to invest around £150 million in three central midfielders, they have already completed two major signings in Youri Tielemans, 29, from Aston Villa in a £35m deal, and Andrey Santos, 22, from Chelsea for £50m.

Prior to Tielemans and Santos' arrival, 21-year-old Kobbie Mainoo was the only established senior central midfielder in the squad.

Daily Mail Sport reported in May that United had earmarked around £80 for a marquee signing to replace the Brazilian, and they saw their No 1 target Elliot Anderson head to Manchester City for a record £116m deal. United also agreed terms with Atlanta for Brazil star Ederson but backed out due to concerns over his knee.

Although Michael Carrick has been talking up the importance of giving United's academy players more opportunities, while Tyler Fletcher and Toby Collyer have seen significant game time during pre-season.

Sports.title: Arsenal make decision over Ethan Nwaneri's future amid interest from Fulham and Everton - after star was left out of Community Shield squad
Sports.content:
Arsenal have decided they would prefer to allow Ethan Nwaneri out on loan rather than a permanent sale.

Mikel Arteta has praised Nwaneri following a difficult loan at Marseille and feels he needs another experience of gaining more competitive game time.

Premier League clubs such as Fulham and Everton checked on the 19-year-old earlier in the summer while RB Leipzig are among a raft of European clubs interested.

He was left out of the matchday squad for the Community Shield win over Manchester City on Sunday but Arsenal are looking to sell others such as Napoli target Gabriel Jesus and Gabriel Martinelli who has interest from Al Sadd among others but wants to either stay or go to a top league if he leaves at all.

Arteta hinted that Ethan Nwaneri could be heading for the exit door prior to the Gunners' victory over City in Cardiff.

He said: ‘It's unquestionable the talent, the desire, the love and the passion he has for the game. It's something that I've always loved about Ethan.

Arsenal would prefer to loan out midfielder Ethan Nwaneri rather than sell him permanently

'I think he's had some great games and he's shown everybody that he has the ability to be here.

‘I want him to be at the club but something that, in the medium-long term, is best for the player as well.

'Ethan needs to play football and if he stays here it’s because we can guarantee that he can have those minutes.

‘Otherwise it's just something that is not good for anybody I think.’

The 19-year-old sat on the Marseille bench in the second half of last season, and has recently been tracked by multiple clubs, including Galatasaray.

Sports.title: Tennis bad boy Nick Kyrgios tests positive for cocaine as he reveals his secret ban and will 'step away from public life to get myself right'
Sports.content:
Tennis bad boy Nick Kyrgios tests positive for cocaine as he reveals his secret ban and will 'step away from public life to get myself right'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Nick Kyrgios has revealed that he has failed a drugs test after testing positive for cocaine and received a provisional suspension.

The former Wimbledon finalist, 31, has endured a checkered few years after suffering persistent injury, and admitted that the toll they have taken on his career gave 'some context' to his failed test.

'I wanted you to hear it from me first,' Kyrgios began his lengthy statement on Instagram. 'I recently failed a drug test in Mallorca after testing positive for cocaine.

'I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it.

'I am sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors, and everyone close to me. Above all, I'm sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I'm deeply disappointed in myself.

'I'm not going to make excuses, but I do want to give some context about where I've been. The last couple of years of injuries have taken a huge toll on me, both physically and mentally. My body hasn't been able to do what my mind expects it to do, and coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined.

Nick Kyrgios has shared that he has failed a drugs test after testing positive for cocaine

The former world No 13 in Brisbane, Australia, in January... he has endured a difficult string of seasons amid persistent injury

'I've always said I didn't choose tennis - tennis chose me. But letting go of something that has been my whole life is one of the hardest things I've ever had to face. At times I've felt helpless and alone.

'None of that excuses what I did.

'However, the good news is that this has given me a wake-up call. For the next 28 days, I'll be stepping away from social media and public life while I focus on getting myself right.

'I'd ask that people respect my privacy during that time, and most importantly the privacy of my family.

'I'm sorry. I'll do the work and come back better. Nick.'

Kyrgios played in Majorca at the Association of Tennis Professionals 250 event in late June, losing his singles match to fellow Australian Adam Walton in straight sets on June 22.

He later withdrew from the doubles, where he and partner John-Patrick Smith had been due to play Austin Krajicek and Nikola Mektic the following day.

Tennis's integrity and anti-doping governing body the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) have since announced that Kyrgios has been handed a mandatory provisional suspension.

'The International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) has provisionally suspended Australian tennis player Nick Kyrgios under the Tennis Anti-Doping Programme,' a statement shared by the organisation read.

'Kyrgios provided a sample during an ATP 250 event in Mallorca, Spain, on 22 June 2026. On 17 July 2026, a World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)-accredited laboratory confirmed the presence of benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

'Cocaine is a stimulant and substance of abuse on the WADA Prohibited List and is banned in competition under the Tennis Anti-Doping Programme. If taken out of competition, reduced sanctions apply for substances of abuse.

Kyrgios in 2022 with Novak Djokovic after losing to the Serb in the Wimbledon final

'Because of the nature of the substance, a provisional suspension is mandatory and has been in place since 4 August 2026.

'Kyrgios, who reached a career-high world singles ranking of 13 in October 2016, has the right to appeal the provisional suspension, but has not done so to date.

'As with all Tennis Anti-Doping Programme cases, ITIA support is available to Kyrgios.

'While suspended, Kyrgios is not allowed to play in, coach at, or attend any events organised or sanctioned by World Tennis, WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams, or any national association.'

Kyrgios reached the Wimbledon final in 2022, losing to the Serbian Novak Djokovic by three sets to one.

It was his only Grand Slam final. His best results in other major tournaments include quarter-final appearances at the US Open in 2022 and the Australian open in 2015.

He is also a Grand Slam doubles champion, winning the 2022 Australian Open with fellow Australian Thanasi Kokkinakis.

Before his suspension, Kyrgios' appearances on the tour had been limited, with the combustible Australian star only taking part in a clutch of events due to his prohibitively high ranking of 919.

Offered wildcards to play events in both singles and doubles, the former world No13 has not won a singles match since last year's Miami Open.

Testing positive for cocaine usage could carry a ban from the sport for up to two years but there is precedent within the sport for a more lenient punishment in light of Kyrgios' admission that he did take the substance. The ban could also be reduced if it was proved that the usage of the drug was not for performance-enhancing benefits.

Former British star Dan Evans was handed a one-year ban in 2017 after testing positive at the Barcelona Open after keeping the drug in the pocket of his washbag.

The International Tennis Federation accepted Evans' explanation that he had become contaminated after the drug found its way onto his finger or medication in the bag accidentally.

Kyrgios' case represents the second high-profile anti-doping revelation in tennis in recent months, after 2023 Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova was handed a four-year ban in June for refusing to take a drugs test.

Sports.title: Dead body found at Charlton Athletic's stadium as club release statement
Sports.content:
Dead body found at Charlton Athletic's stadium as club release statement

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A 33-year-old man was found dead at Charlton Athletic's stadium on Tuesday.

Police officers were called to The Valley stadium on Tuesday morning after an incident, which Charlton say occurred on Monday.

The death is being treated as unexpected, with police investigating whether the man fell from a height.

Daily Mail Sport visited the scene on Wednesday afternoon and there was no longer a police presence at the stadium.

A Metropolitan Police spokesperson said: 'At around 11:15hrs on Tuesday, 18 August, officers attended The Valley stadium on Floyd Road, Charlton following concerns for the welfare of a person.

'Officers attended alongside the London Ambulance Service and located a 33-year-old man, who was sadly pronounced dead at the scene. His next of kin have been informed and continue to be supported.

'Officers are investigating the possibility that the man had fallen from height prior to his death. The death is being treated as unexpected, and an investigation is ongoing.

'Anyone with information is urged to call 101, quoting reference 2809/18AUG.'

The death first came to light in a statement from Charlton on Tuesday evening, which said a body had been discovered at their southeast London stadium.

Charlton said: 'Charlton Athletic are supporting the police with their enquiries following the discovery of a deceased individual at The Valley on Tuesday morning.

'Police were called to the stadium today after an incident that occurred in the early hours of Monday morning. A male was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.

'The death remains under investigation. Anyone with information, or who may have witnessed the incident, is asked to contact police on 101, quoting reference 2809/18AUG.'

A dead body was found at The Valley, home of Charlton Athletic, on Tuesday morning

The statement continued: 'Everyone at Charlton Athletic would like to express their deepest sympathies and heartfelt condolences to the individual's family, friends and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time.

'The club are continuing to assist the authorities with their enquiries and respectfully ask that the privacy of those affected is respected. There is no suggestion of any wrongdoing on the part of the club.

'Charlton Athletic would also like to thank its staff for the professionalism they have shown while dealing with a particularly difficult and distressing situation.'

Charlton played at The Valley on Saturday, beating Derby County 2-1 in their first Championship game of the season.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho reveals Vinicius Jr intervention that wrecked Arsenal transfer plan
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho reveals Vinicius Jr intervention that wrecked Arsenal transfer plan

Vinicius Junior chose to stay at Real Madrid over joining Arsenal with Jose Mounrinho revealing what he told him before a contract extension was signed

View 2 Images Jose Mourinho spoke to Vinicius Junior to make him stay and Real Madrid and snub a transfer to Arsenal (Image: (Photo by INA FASSBENDER / AFP via Getty Images))

Jose Mourinho has revealed he told Vinicius Junior that leaving Real Madrid for Arsenal was "not worth it". The Brazil international was strongly linked with a move to Emirates Stadium before he chose to to sign a contract extension after a meeting between his agents, the Real hierarchy and Mourinho.

‌



The 26-year-old had less than a year left on his previous deal with negotiations over fresh terms stalling due to his salary demands. Ultimately, Los Blancos agreed to meet his wage requirements and he is now contracted to the club until 2032.

‌



Ahead of the new season, Mourinho spoke on a number topics to Spanish outlet El Chiringuito TV with Vinicius discussed. "Obviously I talked to him, but Vinicius has fallen in love with Real Madrid," Mourinho revealed.

‌



"The only thing I told him was: 'Vini, where do you want to go? You’ve only been in Brazil and you only know Real Madrid… You only understand Real Madrid when you leave. When you leave, that’s when you realise what Real Madrid is. Don’t leave. It’s not worth it'."

"I think what he has felt in terms of the group’s growth, the way we’ve been working and developing, has given him a very important feeling," Mourinho added. "Vinicius is another machine – it’s a pleasure to watch him work. We have a lot of quality."

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Arsenal pivoted to a sensational deal for Vinicius after Chelsea signed Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for £117million. Following his decision, a defensive addition seemingly became the priority with links to Jarell Quansah of Bayer Leverkusen and Barcelona's Jules Kounde emerging.

Aston Villa star Ezri Konsa remained the club's top target throughout and according to The Athletic, Arsenal are closing in on signing him.

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa is set to join Arsenal

‌



With owners from both club's now involved to negotiate a final fee, the deal is advancing. Arsenal face a race against time to have him registered for their opening clash of the season against Coventry on Friday night.

Even if the relevant documents are complete by 12pm, he is unlikely to feature having not yet had a pre-season due to his participation in the World Cup.

Konsa played alongside Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke for England and mostly played at centre-back but did feature at right-back. His versatility is a key attribute and something Arteta prefers all of his defenders to have.

Sports.title: Meet the red-hot Mauritian cyclist bidding to banish injury demons on Lloyds Tour of Britain stage
Sports.content:
Meet the red-hot Mauritian cyclist bidding to banish injury demons on Lloyds Tour of Britain stage

Kimberley Le Court-Pienaar won stage one of the UCI Women’s WorldTour stage race last year, but a crash on stage two saw her unable to continue a day later

View 2 Images Kimberley Le Court-Pienaar is part of the AG Insurance - Soudal Team (Image: © SWpix.com (t/a Photography Hub Ltd))

Kimberley Le Court-Pienaar still feels the nerves that led her to swear she would never ride the Lloyds Tour of Britain again - but the desire for redemption is stronger.

‌



The Mauritian AG Insurance-Soudal rider won stage one of the UCI Women’s WorldTour stage race last year, but a crash on stage two saw her unable to continue a day later.

‌



It has been another injury-hit year for Le Court-Pienaar, who sustained a fractured wrist at the Tour of Flanders in April, but a stage win at the Tour de France Femmes has proven that comebacks are becoming her thing.

‌



“When I finished last year, I told the team I didn't want to come back,” admitted the 30-year-old.

“It really scared me because of the experience I've had. But then throughout the year, we discussed it and we saw that the route is a really nice route.

“Me and my teammate Gladys [Verhulst Wild], who also had a horrendous crash last year, are both here and we want to not have that page in the book where it's a question mark.

‌



“We want to turn the page and have it green. We want to redeem ourselves and come back and have revenge. That’s why we're here.”

View 2 Images The Lloyds Tour of Britain Women starts in Cockermouth on Wednesday 19 August (Image: © SWpix.com (t/a Photography Hub Ltd))

Le Court-Pienaar suffered a bone bruise and skin abrasion on her sacrum after her crash last year but re-enters again as one of the favourites for the largest free-to-attend sporting spectacle in the UK.

‌



But despite becoming the first African to don the Tour de France Femmes’ yellow jersey in 2025, she will still have to overcome the anxieties that affect even the very best on her return to British roads.

“You get a bit traumatised by things like that. Also, since my crash in Flanders, it's always been a bit of a scare,” Le Court-Pienaar added.

“My wrist is still a bit sensitive. It's not fully healed yet. So, of course, you get a bit scared if you do something funny or something happens and you fall again.

‌



“Coming back to a race where you DNF’d from a crash is not always ideal. But I think coming back and trying to finish it off in a good way is the best way you can climb over that obstacle.”

It was an approach Le Court-Pienaar applied in the Tour de France Femmes, where her stage six victory came following a mechanical failure during the race.

Having also crashed early in the stage, she fought her way back to bridge to a breakaway group before beating Cédrine Kerbaol to the line with a sprint.

‌



“I like doing things for other people and making people proud and happy more than I want to do it for myself. That's just how I am,” Le Court-Pienaar explained.

“When I won in the Tour, the team did an insane job. Without them, I would not come back to the peloton while saving the amount of energy I saved to go further and get the stage win.

“To be able to give that back to them and get the stage win is the best feeling I could ever have.

Article continues below

“It’s proof that never giving up is how things should go. If you have a bad moment in the race, it doesn't mean it's over.”

Sports.title: British cyclist Anna Morris leads tributes to Finlay Tarling as Lloyds Tour of Britain gets underway
Sports.content:
British cyclist Anna Morris leads tributes to Finlay Tarling as Lloyds Tour of Britain gets underway

Tarling died following an incident at the Volta a Portugal last week with riders taking part in a minute’s applause ahead of the Tour’s start in Cockermouth in his memory

View Image Finlay Tarling has sadly passed away following a serious accident in Portugal. (Image: (Photo by Huw Fairclough/Getty Images))

Anna Morris will keep Finlay Tarling in her thoughts when she clips in to race the Lloyds Tour of Britain this week, after riders took part in a tribute to the Welsh rider ahead of stage one.

‌



Tarling died following an incident at the Volta a Portugal last week with riders taking part in a minute’s applause ahead of the Tour’s start in Cockermouth in his memory.

‌



At just 19 years old, the Welsh rider from Ceredigion represented a highly respected figure in the sport, with his brother Josh, 22, competing for Great Britain.

‌



“We had some really sad news with Fin last week. That’s really hit the cycling world hard, at Welsh, British and world level because the Tarling's are a huge presence in cycling,” said Morris.

“I’ll definitely be riding with lots of thoughts in my head this week. The Tarling family have said Fin loved riding and racing his bike so when we clip in this week, we will definitely have him in our thoughts.”

Morris enters the Lloyds Tour of Britain off the back of a Commonwealth Games that saw her bag three medals, including two golds in the individual pursuit and points race.

‌



The 31-year-old was part of a Welsh cycling contingent who showed their strength on the track at Glasgow 2026, finishing second in the medal table in the velodrome with six golds in total, only behind Australia.

Having won the North Yorkshire Grand Prix on her return to the road, Morris is among those billed to continue to show that Welsh strength on home roads.

“It’s amazing seeing the strength and depth we have in Wales. It’s super exciting to have a couple of stages in Wales,” said the Cardiff-born rider.

‌



“We’ve had national road championships for the past two years and we’ve got it again next year and then some of the Tour de France going through Wales as well next year.

“So, Welsh cycling is in a really good place at the moment. We’ve got some strong Welsh riders racing this week and I’m excited to see the likes of Zoe Bäckstedt and see what they can do.”

Fresh from a debut Tour de France Femmes, Pontyclun’s Bäckstedt enters the UCI Women’s WorldTour event as one of the favourites and will benefit from home support through stages three and four with Great Orme and Llanidloes featuring as stops.

‌



“When you hear your name at the side of the road, it picks you up in the tough moments. We’re racing over hours and hours so you go through a lot of different emotions and I’m excited to have that support beside the road,” explained Morris.

Carmarthen’s Jess Roberts also hits the road for the Great Britain Cycling Team alongside Morris, having won silver and bronze at the Commonwealth Games.

While she bids to maintain fitness for her endeavours on the track, she represents another to watch for Welsh crowds at the largest free-to-attend sporting spectacle in the UK.

Article continues below

“I’m so proud to be Welsh, it’s just nice to showcase Wales,” said the 27-year-old. “We’re quite a small country and there are going to be some hard stages there. We’re all proud to be Welsh and showing that off is nice.”

Sports.title: Arsenal close in on deal to sign Aston Villa and England defender Ezri Konsa
Sports.content:
Arsenal close in on deal to sign Aston Villa and England defender Ezri Konsa

Arsenal failed with a £40million bid for Aston Villa star Ezri Konsa earlier in the summer transfer window, but talks between the clubs have now progressed towards a resolution

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa is set to leave Aston Villa (Image: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

Arsenal are close to striking a deal with Aston Villa to sign Ezri Konsa. The Gunners are in the market for a right-sided defender and Konsa, 28, is their preferred target.

‌



Both William Saliba and Jurrien Timber will miss the start of the Premier League season with long-term injuries, reducing Mikel Arteta's options. Konsa's ability to play at centre-back as well as right-back appeals to Arteta, who appreciates versatile defenders.

‌



The Athletic report that although the deal isn't done, talks are now advancing. There has been dialogue at ownership level to reduce gap in valuations.

‌



Arsenal have been willing to pay £40million for Konsa, with Villa rating him closer to £60m. Meanwhile, personal terms are not expected to be an issue.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



The England international was heavily involved at the World Cup, starting all but one of the their eight fixtures. The only game which he didn't start was England's 2-1 semi-final loss against Argentina, coming on as a 72nd-minute substitute.

Konsa has two years left on his contract with Villa, who handed him a five-year deal in 2023. The 28-year-old didn't feature in pre-season for Villa, having been granted extra time off following England's campaign in North America.

Villa begin their Premier League season away to Brighton on Sunday, having already lost three key players this summer despite qualifying for the Champions League. Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne have all departed for a combined £159.5m.

‌



How much is Ezri Konsa worth? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa impressed for England this summer (Image: Johnny Fidelin/Icon Sport via Getty Images)

Team-mates Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez could also leave before the transfer window closes on Monday, September 1. Villa announced two signings on Wednesday morning, welcoming Atletico Madrid left-back Matteo Ruggeri (£17m) and Parma goalkeeper Zion Suzuki (£30m).

‌



Arsenal are set to become the latest club to raid Villa, with Arteta confirming after Sunday's 3-0 victory over Manchester City in the Community Shield that he wants more signings. "We know that there are certain areas that, through injuries, we are weaker and we need to strengthen," the Gunners boss admitted.

"We are trying to do that, we've been trying to do that for weeks so only the right opportunity and the club is available to do it, we will do it."

Arteta previously said: "What I can tell you is the ambition of the club, it's big, we want to improve the squad, we want to evolve the squad, and in order to achieve that, we have obviously detected some areas that can be strengthened. That's what we are trying to do."
