World.title: Amanal Petros: From refugee to European champion
World.content:
Amanal Petros fled to Germany as a teenager. Now one of the world's top marathon runners, he recently won gold at the European Athletics Championships.

Amanal Petros stood in Birmingham's Victoria Square, the German flag draped over his shoulders and the gold medal resting on his chest. Eleven months after narrowly missing out on a World Championship title in Tokyo, the 31-year-old had just won his first major marathon.

After roughly 25 of the 42 kilometers, Petros picked up the pace on an incline, breaking up the lead pack. No one could keep up with him. He was able to savor the victory during the final 2 kilometers. He crossed the finish line in 2:09:11 — a record time for the men's marathon at the European Athletics Championships.

"My goal was to wrap things up early," Petros said afterwards. "That worked out perfectly."

The fact that Italian runner Pietro Riva finished just seven seconds behind him hardly reflected the commanding nature of the victory. "I had everything under control," Petros added.

Late arrival

Issues entering the United Kingdom meant Petros didn't arrive in Birmingham until Saturday — the day before the race. Media reports indicated there were difficulties with his electronic travel authorization.

"It took a very, very long time; it was awful. We were traveling back and forth for two days," he recounted. The German Athletics Association (DLV) helped resolve the issues.

The following day, a course featuring eight laps, inclines and numerous turns awaited the runners. Petros had spent months preparing for the event at altitude in Kenya.

"120 turns, the climbs. It was a huge challenge," he said after the race. Then Petros dedicated the gold medal to his mother.

"She is my queen and my source of strength," he stressed. "Thinking of her gives me new energy and motivation. She is simply the best."

His mother lives more than 5,000 kilometers (3,107 miles) away in the Tigray region of Ethiopia.

Coming to Germany alone at 16

Petros was born in the Eritrean port city of Assab in 1995. As a young child, he fled with his family — escaping the war between Eritrea and Ethiopia — to Tigray in northern Ethiopia. He grew up there with his two younger sisters. Beginning at the age of 5, he worked in the fields and tended to the animals.

Amanal Petros broke the German men's marathon record earlier this year Image: Sebastian Gollnow/dpa/picture alliance

Petros left Ethiopia alone at the age of 16, arriving in Germany in early 2012. He was initially housed in accommodation for asylum-seekers. His mother and sisters remained in Tigray.

In late 2021, due to the conflict in the region, Petros went more than two months without any contact with them.

"It's very hard," he told DW at the time. "Sometimes I sleep poorly and have bad dreams. But I try not to give up hope."

Running helped. "If I were to give up my sport, I would have lost everything," Petros said. "I've already lost my family, and then I would have lost the last thing I have left."

The situation in Tigray weighed on his mind even during races.

"I think about my family all the time," Petros said in 2021. While running, he tries to block out those thoughts and focus on the sport.

Talent discovered on the football pitch

Shortly after he arrived in Germany, Petros started playing football, but a club official noticed his pace and hooked him up with a local athletics club. In June 2012, just months after his arrival, Petros ran his first 10-kilometer race, winning by around two and a half minutes.

Getting acclimatized to a hew country wasn't so easy.

"Learning the language was a major challenge," Petros told DW back then. "But understanding the German mentality was an even bigger one."

He was naturalized in 2015, although at the time immigrants were usually required to wait eight years to become eligible for German citizenship. At the 2021 Olympic Games in Japan, he competed for Germany in the marathon for the first time.

In the years that followed, Petros moved closer to the international elite. In December 2025, he ran a time of 2:04:03 in Valencia, setting a new German marathon record. Another German record followed in March at the Berlin Half Marathon, where he clocked 59:22 minutes.

Petros lost in a photo finish at the 2025 World Championships in Tokyo Image: Kyodo News/IMAGO

Near miss at Worlds

Just how close Petros had come to the world elite was evident at the World Championships in Tokyo in September 2025.

Picking up the pace with 350 meters to go, he was the first to enter the stadium and, on the home straight looked like the new world champion. But Alphonce Simbu of Tanzania passed him in the closing meters of the race. Both were clocked at 2:09:48. The photo finish decided the outcome: Petros missed gold by 0.03 seconds.

"As a professional athlete, I simply have to accept that and look ahead," Petros said afterwards. With silver, he secured Germany's first World Championship medal in the men's marathon since 1983.

"Achieving this is a huge deal for me, especially for my family, for my mom," he said after the race. He planned to send her videos of his run. "Hopefully, I'll be able to bring her to Germany for a competition someday."

Running talent from Ethiopia To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Now, 11 months after that photo-finish loss in Tokyo, Petros has savored his first major international title in Birmingham.

"The race was incredibly, incredibly hard," Petros said. "But a bit of red wine will get me back on my feet quickly."

And just how much is "a bit"?

"Oh, you know, one, two, or three glasses."

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: Fact check: How do I spot fake social media accounts, bots and trolls?
World.content:
If you are unsure whether to trust a message on TikTok or X, study its source. The following indicators can help you determine if you are dealing with a fake account, bot or troll.

Hundreds of thousands of inauthentic social media accounts. Tens of thousands of fake articles. Millions of automated posts.

These are some of the figures cited by the German Foreign Ministry in connection with a Russian disinformation campaign that was first detected in 2022, after Russia invaded Ukraine.

Known as Doppelgänger, the operation aimed to amplify pro-Russian narratives on social media platforms in countries like Germany.

On some days, thousands of the accounts were active, posting more than once per second in a coordinated manner, the ministry said in a 2024 report.

This campaign underscores just how important it is for users to verify the authenticity of social media accounts and identify when content is being published or amplified by bots and trolls.

But first, what’s the difference between a bot and a troll? And how can you spot them?

DW Fact check offers tips to help you navigate today's information landscape.

What are fake accounts?

Look at the account's name, but also check the URL and the follower numbers

Fake accounts are social media profiles that conceal their true identity. Some may pretend to be ordinary users; others can impersonate politicians, institutions or journalists.

Not all fake accounts have malicious intent. Some people may use pseudonyms to protect their identity or for security reasons. Activists or whistleblowers may use fake accounts to investigate sensitive issues.

What are bots?

Bots, short for robots, tirelessly comment on posts, share content, or artificially stoke online debate on marginal or otherwise overlooked topics. Sometimes, they’re entirely innocent, but sometimes they’re intent is harmful.

Good bots may automatically share news or weather forecasts, as well as earthquake alerts and satellite images on social media.

Bad bots, in contrast, are designed to imitate genuine human activity to advance a certain agenda. Depending on the algorithm, such computer programs may compose and publish social media posts or comments, follow others, or even send out friendship requests.

Bad bots can distort reality by amplifying certain political opinions on social media platforms and drawing artificial attention to certain issues.

What are trolls?

Troll accounts are harder to detect than downright fake accounts, as they are usually controlled by real human beings Image: Jan Eifert/picture alliance

Trolls, on the other hand, are real human beings who exhibit destructive and hyperactive online behavior.

Some are even paid to harass certain public figures or media organizations as part of so-called troll factories or farms.

One of the most prominent examples of a troll factory is the Internet Research Agency in St. Petersburg, Russia.

EUvsDisinfo , a project by the European External Action Service to counter disinformation, found that the agency had disseminated falsehoods and pro-Kremlin messages in multiple languages during various European and US election campaigns and in the lead-up to several referenda.

How can you spot them?

Many of the fake accounts, bots and trolls may disappear before you even notice them.

At least in Europe, social media platforms are required under the Digital Services Act (DSA) to release transparency reports, including how much content they delete.

In the last three months of 2025, for instance, Meta reported taking action on 1.1 billion accounts.

But sometimes accounts appear faster than platforms can take action. So here are some concrete tips than can help you identify them.

Identity: Check the account name, profile picture and handle

A blue check mark once signalled a verified identity. On some platforms, they can now be bought, making it harder to tell who is really behind an account. Image: MAURO PIMENTEL/AFP

Genuine accounts tend to have a consistent digital identity. Their name, profile picture, bio and content generally tend to support the same story about who’s behind the account.

Be cautious if this does not appear to be the case. Potential red flags include:

A generic, stock-style or AI-generated profile picture

A username containing a long string of seemingly random characters and numbers

An account that was created recently and suddenly became very active

A generic bio, such as “Truth Seeker” or “Patriot”, with little or no personal information

Beyond this, verify the information through official channels.

Public figures typically have a traceable online presence. Look for links to official websites and organizations they work for. Check whether the account’s name, profile picture, personal information and handle are consistent with information published elsewhere.

Use the reverse image search method (for example on Google Lens or TinEye ) to find out whether the picture used in the profile depicts someone else than claimed, or if the image has surfaced elsewhere online.

And don’t rely on verification badges. While a blue check mark was once primarily used to confirm the identity of public figures and organizations, some platforms now allow users to buy them.

Behavior: Review what the account posts

Public figures typically have a traceable online presence Image: David Talukdar/ZUMA/picture alliance

Fake accounts, bots and troll accounts often behave differently from ordinary users.

Genuine users typically interact with others, discuss several topics and display natural patterns of activity that are often connected to their interests, profession or geographical location.

A German student posting images purporting to show an Afghan war zone? A Russian pensioner sharing photos from what she claims are Parisian anti-vaccination protests?

Neither is impossible, but both may warrant closer scrutiny. The accounts could be fake or they may be sharing disinformation. Suspicious behavior like this is typical of bots, too.

Bots also tend to post at a speed and frequency that would be nearly impossible for most people to sustain.

Trolls accounts, meanwhile, are harder to detect than downright fake accounts, as they are usually controlled by real human beings.

For trolls, it’s best to focus on the content they’re sharing. A troll’s defining feature is often their behavior rather than their identity.

Trolls are usually less interested in meaningful discussion than in provoking reactions. Their goal is frequently to increase engagement by generating outrage, sowing divisions or derailing conversations.

Network: Examine the account’s network and interactions

A few minutes spent examining an account’s identity, behavior and network can go a long way towards helping you distinguish genuine users from fake accounts Image: Tim Wegner/epd-bild/picture alliance

Fake accounts, bots and trolls rarely operate in isolation. You can find valuable clues about an account’s authenticity by examining who follows it and how other users interacts with it.

Genuine users tend to have a diverse mix of followers and interactions. By contrast, fake accounts are often part of networks that repeatedly amplify a particular narrative.

Here are some potential red flags:

Large numbers of followers with generic profile information

Comments or replies that are repetitive, identical or unrelated to the content of the post

Thousands of followers but little meaningful engagement

Followers that were created recently, have little posting history, or primarily repost content from other accounts

Conversations that appear one-sided, with little disagreement or diversity of opinions

Multiple accounts posting the same comments, links or hashtags within a short period

If you are unsure whether an account is fake, or whether content is being spread by a bot or a troll, slow down and take a closer look.

A few minutes spent examining an account’s identity, behavior and network can go a long way towards helping you distinguish genuine users from fake accounts, bots and trolls.

This article was first published in 2022 and has been revised to incorporate new developments and trends. Edited by Josh Axelrod.

This article is part of a DW Fact check series on digital literacy. Other articles include:

And here you can read more about how DW fact-checks fake news.

World.title: El anuncio del éxito de la primera vacuna contra el melanoma dispara las acciones de Moderna y Merck
World.content:
El avance se ha difundido en una nota de prensa en la que no se ofrecen datos concretos de mejora de supervivencia. De confirmarse, se trataría de un hito histórico

Las farmacéuticas Moderna y MSD (conocida como Merck) han anunciado que su ensayo de fase 3 (el previo a la aprobación de un fármaco) de su vacuna personalizada contra el melanoma, que aún sigue en marcha, ha alcanzado el éxito en varios de sus hitos. Aunque en la nota de prensa que han difundido para publicitar el resultado no hay datos sobre cuánto se ha incrementado la supervivencia o cuánto se han reducido las posibilidades de recaída, en ella se afirma que la combinación de la vacuna (intismeran autogene) con una inmunoterapia (pembrolizumab) alcanzó los objetivos de supervivencia libre de recaída y sin que el cáncer se extienda a otros órganos. Tras la publicación de la nota, las acciones de Moderna se llegaron a disparar un 87% y las de MSD un 8%.

A falta de conocer detalles, se trata de un hito histórico porque es la primera vez que una vacuna de este tipo logra un resultado positivo en un ensayo de fase 3, el más avanzado. Y también es la primera vez que lo hace un tratamiento oncológico basado en ARN mensajero, la misma tecnología que sirvió para hacer las vacunas frente al covid.

Como referencia, en el ensayo anterior en el que se probó este tratamiento, que se presentó el pasado junio en el congreso de la Sociedad Estadounidense de Oncología Médica (ASCO), se logró reducir un 49% el riesgo de recaída o muerte y un 59% el riesgo de metástasis.

El nuevo tratamiento se probó en pacientes con melanoma (el cáncer de piel más peligroso) a los que ya se había extirpado el tumor quirúrgicamente, pero que tenían un riesgo alto de recaída. En el ensayo, participaron 1.137 personas divididas en dos grupos. Un tercio recibió pembrolizumab, una inmunoterapia de efectividad comprobada, y a dos tercios de los pacientes recibieron la vacuna personalizada a la inmunoterapia.

La vacuna no funciona exactamente como las que se utilizan contra los virus, que se fabrican en masa y a todo el mundo le funcionan más o menos igual y se utilizan como protección frente a la enfermedad. En este caso, se elabora de forma personalizada para el cáncer de una persona una vez que ha aparecido. Se analiza una muestra del tumor extirpado al paciente para identificar sus características únicas y con esta información se diseña una vacuna de ARN mensajero a medida. Esa vacuna enseña al sistema inmunitario del paciente a reconocer y atacar sus células cancerosas concretas en caso de que reaparezcan.

Tras este primer anuncio, MSD y Moderna presentarán los datos completos en un congreso médico internacional y empezarán a hablar con las autoridades reguladoras para pedir la aprobación del tratamiento. Además, ambas compañías tienen ya en marcha ocho ensayos más con la misma tecnología de vacunas personalizadas en otros tipos de cáncer como pulmón, vejiga y riñón.

[Habrá actualización]

World.title: Fallece Josep Cusí, fiel amigo de Juan Carlos I
World.content:
Josep Cusí, el fiel amigo de Juan Carlos I, ha fallecido este miércoles en Barcelona a los 92 años. Discreto empresario, fue el armador de los bribones, los barcos de regatas del rey emérito, pero sobre todo uno de sus confidentes más discretos después de conocerle a principios de los años sesenta durante una cacería organizada por el dictador Francisco Franco, de quien fue instructor de tiro y compañero de caza. Cusí padeció a finales de 2021 un ictus que, tras dejarle un mes en estado de coma, le causó problemas de movilidad y deterioró de forma ostensible su estado de salud, complicada todavía más estos últimos días.

El empresario tenía un variado currículum. Ingeniero electrónico de formación, empresario, y nadador y waterpolista de competición, si bien acudió a los Juegos Olímpicos de México en 1968 para participar en la competición de tiro. Y era uno de esos discretos miembros de viejo cuño que acostumbran a integrar la burguesía catalana, asociado del Real Club Náutico de Barcelona o del Círculo del Liceo. Estaba casado en terceras nupcias con Inés Muiños, hija de un prestigioso oftalmólogo de la clínica especializada barcelonesa Barraquer, y tenía seis hijos.

Él se consideraba un aventurero. A los 18 años se embarcó durante tres meses en el barco Calypso del oceanógrafo Jacques Costeau e incluso participó en el documental El mar del silencio. Aquella singladura le permitió obtener la medalla de Legión de Honor de manos del presidente francés Jacques de Gaulle. Entre otros reconocimientos figuran la medalla al mérito deportivo y la Gran Cruz del Mérito Naval.

Aunque es conocida de sobras su relación con Juan Carlos I, Josep Cusí, que ha salido fotografiado en múltiples ocasiones junto al monarca, el diario The Telegraph desveló hace seis años que Cusí había sido el encargado de compartir a medias con el rey emérito el viaje nupcial de los actuales reyes de España, Felipe VI y Letizia, que se acercó al medio millón de dólares. Fruto de esa buena relación, Cusí rompió en 2018 su discreción habitual para, en un acto de la Fundación Elena Barraquer, defender la buena relación que mantenía la actual reina con su predecesora en el cargo y suegra, Sofía. En todo caso, con quien él ha mantenido hasta el último momento una cerrada relación ha sido con Juan Carlos I.

Pese a conocer de antes, su relación se intensifica cuando el monarca visita Barcelona para preparar los Juegos Olímpicos de 1972. Cusí fue uno de los ayudantes del equipo español y un año antes de la cita olímpica empezaba a surcar las aguas el primer Bribón, barco que era entonces de Cusí, mientras que Juan Carlos de borbón lo hace con un barco similar denominado Shere-Kan. Sería la última vez que competirían por separado. En 1972 se unirían en el Bribón II, cada uno con papeles muy definidos: el futuro rey tomaría el mando como patrón; Cusí la intendencia —incluida la selección de veteranos y discretos tripulantes— como armador. Esos barcos de regatas han ganado diversas competiciones en sus cuatro décadas de navegación. En 2007 se estrenó la última unidad de los bribones (hasta 2011 duró), aunque no el último barco que financiaria el empresario catalán al monarca. ¿Por qué ese nombre? “Porque para competir es necesario ser sagaz, agresivo y también un poco pillo”. Bribón también se llama el perro que ha acompañado los últimos años de su vida a Cusí, un regalo del rey.

La periodista Pilar Urbano, en su libro Genio y figura, relató que la buena relación entre ambos amigos había pasado por “algún bajón cuando don Juan Carlos pretendía acudir a alguna de las reuniones acompañado de Corina Sayn-Wittgenstein”. Cusí explicó en un artículo publicado en La Vanguardia en 2012 que compartía con la confesión de Juan Carlos I que la decisión de acudir a un safari de caza en Botsuana, por el que tuvo que ser evacuado tras romperse la cadera, “no fue una decisión acertada”. Entonces señaló que “que hay que evitar los tropiezos, en las escaleras de un bungalow y en la vida pública”, extremo que intentó llevar al extremo siempre que su temperamento se lo permitiera. En todo caso, en 1983 dijo sobre su relación con el rey: “Yo no me considero su patrón, sino su servidor, en el mar y en la tierra, dentro y fuera del Bribón”.

La carrera empresarial de Cusí es la más desconocida. Con 16 años, explica Efe, entró en el negocio familiar de componentes electrónicos y participó en la iluminación de varios lugares emblemáticos de Barcelona, como la Font Màgica de Montjuïc o las iglesias del Tibidabo y de Santa Maria del Mar. A sus 65 años, decidió vender la empresa.

World.title: El ejército de Israel admite que disparó contra el coche de la niña palestina Hind Rajab en Gaza y abre una investigación penal por su muerte
World.content:
Las Fuerzas Armadas también abren pesquisas sobre la muerte de 15 trabajadores humanitarios y de emergencia en la Franja, y cierran la del asesinato de los trabajadores de la ONG del chef José Andrés

El ejército israelí abrirá investigaciones penales internas sobre las muertes de la niña palestina Hind Rajab en Gaza en enero de 2024 y de 15 trabajadores humanitarios y de emergencia en marzo de 2025 en Rafah, que trató de ocultar enterrando los vehículos en los que acudieron a atender heridos, según anunció el miércoles. Es un tipo de investigación interna que rara vez resulta en condena, pero muestra la importancia que han cobrado estos casos. Cierra en cambio otro de alto perfil: el asesinato de siete trabajadores humanitarios de World Central Kitchen, la organización benéfica del chef José Andrés, cuando iban en una carretera de Gaza, en abril de 2024.

Son las resoluciones sobre cinco incidentes relacionados con la muerte de palestinos, tras el análisis de su Mecanismo de Investigación y Evaluación. Respecto a este incidente, el ejército afirmó que no existía ninguna sospecha razonable de conducta delictiva que justificara la apertura de una investigación penal.

“Durante más de mil días, las Fuerzas Armadas de Israel han librado intensos combates en numerosos frentes, llevando a cabo una amplia gama de misiones militares en una realidad operativa excepcionalmente compleja”, según declaró el ejército israelí. Como parte de sus obligaciones conforme al derecho internacional y la legislación israelí, investigan incidentes excepcionales ocurridos durante el combate, añadió el ejército.

World.title: Consumo sanciona a la empresa de alquiler de coches Avis con un millón de euros por cobrar la gestión de multas
World.content:
El Ministerio de Consumo ha multado a la empresa de alquiler de vehículos Avis con un millón de euros por lo que considera “prácticas abusivas”. Desde el departamento que lidera Pablo Bustinduy aseguran que la tasa en concepto de gastos de gestión de sanción administrativa que cobra la compañía cuando algún cliente es multado “establece una carga económica desproporcionada que rompe el equilibrio contractual en perjuicio de la persona consumidora”. Lo que ha motivado una sanción por vulnerar la Ley General para la Defensa de los Consumidores y Usuarios.

El ministerio asegura que el recargo, que tiene como objetivo gestionar el pago de la multa y comunicar a la Administración la identidad de la persona infractora, contraviene la ley porque este trámite lo debe acometer obligatoriamente la empresa. Consumo detalla que “la identificación del conductor responsable de una infracción constituye una obligación legal del titular del vehículo” de acuerdo con el artículo 11 de la ley sobre Tráfico, Circulación de Vehículos a Motor y Seguridad Vial. En el caso de estas empresas, esta obligación se cumple facilitando a la Administración la identidad de la persona arrendataria o, en su caso, el contrato de alquiler. Avis cobra entre 33,88 y 45 euros a los clientes sancionados mientras usaban sus coches de alquiler por realizar esta gestión.

Por ello, el departamento liderado por Bustinduy concluye que se han vulnerado los artículos 82, 87.5 y 87.6 (relativos a cláusulas abusivas) de la ley que protege los derechos de los consumidores. A este hecho se añade la concurrencia de una “circunstancia agravante al persistir en una práctica declarada previamente ilícita”, lo que justifica la multa de un millón de euros. Consumo se refiere a que un juzgado de Vitoria declaró en septiembre de 2020 “abusiva” esta cláusula y condenó a la empresa a eliminarla, algo que no ha hecho, según destaca Consumo.

La compañía recoge en su página web que cobra “una tasa administrativa, independiente del importe de la sanción para cubrir los gastos que conlleva el procedimiento”. Avis destaca que el cargo de la tasa administrativa se realiza desde el momento en que se recibe la notificación de la multa. Para evitar este cargo, la empresa informa de que “es necesario” realizar el pago de la multa “previo a la notificación”.

El procedimiento sancionador del ministerio comenzó con una denuncia presentada por la Asociación Vasca de Personas Consumidoras y Usuarias (Acuv). El 16 de octubre de 2024, esta organización denunció ante el ministerio que Avis —junto a otra empresa del sector, Sixt, sobre la que Consumo no confirma si hay algún expediente abierto— estaba incluyendo en sus contratos de alquiler estas comisiones. En la denuncia solicitaba una sanción por un incumplimiento grave de la normativa tras recibir “numerosas quejas” de personas afectadas. A ello, Acuv añadía el hecho de que “estas cláusulas ya fueron declaradas abusivas en su momento” por una sentencia que obligaba a “dejar de aplicarlas en los contratos vigentes y abstenerse de incorporarlas en el futuro”.

La decisión del ministerio agota la vía administrativa, pero no la judicial. Consumo señala que Avis puede recurrir la sanción en los tribunales correspondientes.

World.title: Estrategia de EE UU en crisis en Asia-Pacífico
World.content:
Desde su llegada a la Casa Blanca, los analistas de política exterior han insistido en la importancia de centrarse en las acciones de Donald Trump y no en su retórica. La reciente orden del presidente estadounidense de reducir sustancialmente las maniobras militares conjuntas con Corea del Sur envía una señal que ni Seúl ni el conjunto de la región pueden ignorar. Es la enésima manifestación de un patrón que pasa por la adopción de medidas de presión y castigo sobre sus aliados mientras estrecha la relación personal con líderes autoritarios. El episodio arroja dudas sobre la política de seguridad nacional de EE UU en Asia-Pacífico frente al creciente poder militar de China, al tiempo que recuerda a los aliados la necesidad de hacerse cargo de su propia defensa con la mayor rapidez posible.

Trump reprocha a Seúl que se negara a sumarse a la operación contra Irán y que no haya puesto en marcha ninguno de los proyectos de inversión por 350.000 millones de dólares a los que se comprometió en el acuerdo comercial con EE UU para evitar la imposición de aranceles. Asume a cambio el argumentario de Pyongyang de que se trata de operaciones “inapropiadas y hostiles”.

EE UU y Corea del Sur han realizado ejercicios militares anuales desde hace más de 70 años, una pieza decisiva del andamiaje que ha sostenido la península de Corea desde 1953 y de la arquitectura defensiva de Asia-Pacífico. Sirven para disuadir a potenciales adversarios, en este caso a Corea del Norte, pero también para mostrar cohesión entre los aliados frente a la amenaza china, mejorar la interoperabilidad de las fuerzas militares y reafirmar el compromiso de seguridad de Washington con la región. Una estrategia que ahora queda definitivamente cuestionada.

Este mes, el portaaviones USS George Washington zarpó del Pacífico con rumbo al mar Arábigo, lo que deja a la región sin la presencia de ningún portaaviones estadounidense. En marzo, el Pentágono retiró de Corea del Sur parte del sistema de defensa antimisiles THAAD —una importante capa de las defensas aéreas del país— al reorientar de nuevo sus recursos hacia Oriente Próximo.

Las maniobras militares suponen un innegable coste económico y de munición y ahí queda en evidencia el impacto de la guerra con Irán sobre los arsenales estadounidenses. La situación ha puesto en alerta a sus aliados, que ven cómo se retrasan los envíos de armas, incluidos los misiles Tomahawk a Japón y la histórica venta de armas a Taiwán, ante las protestas de Pekín. Si alguien puede mostrarse satisfecho con este giro de guion es el presidente chino, Xi Jinping, quien viajará a Washington dentro de cinco semanas.

World.title: De Edna O’Brien a Juan José Saer, cinco libros de verano para leer en otoño
World.content:
El verano parece invitar a ciertas lecturas, pero estos cinco libros no caducan el 31 de agosto. Entre ellos hay clásicos universales de autores ya fallecidos como Virginia Woolf y obras de clásicos muy contemporáneos como Edna O’Brien. Sus historias van de De Madrid al Río de la Plata y desde Dublín hasta Venecia.

La larga espera del ángel, de Melania G. Mazzucco La vida de Tintoretto se cruza con la de su hija y con la de su ciudad en este adictivo novelón histórico que es libro de familia, de arte y de geografía. ¿Contraindicaciones? Usted querrá viajar a Venecia ipso facto. Si no se resiste, vaya a la Scuola Grande di San Rocco. Las chicas de campo, de Edna O'Brien Frente al ataque de nostalgia que le ha dado este agosto al volver temporalmente al pueblo, esta novela perfecta —íntima y cáustica— le recordará por qué se fueron de allí sus padres, sus madres y sus amigas. Pasa en la Irlanda profunda, pero sirve para todas las profundidades. Las olas, de Virginia Woolf ¿Novela, poema, ensayo psicológico? Este libro revolucionario exige una concentración a prueba de alertas de móvil, pero merece mucho la pena. Eso sí, una vez que se sumerja en el libro, no podrá dejarlo. El siglo XX se empeñó en crear una obra total que trascendiera los géneros. Aquí la tienen. El río sin orillas, de Juan José Saer Claudio Magris se inventó un género recorriendo el Danubio —cuando tenía agua— desde el nacimiento hasta la desembocadura y Saer imitó la fórmula con el Río de la Plata, pero a la inversa. El resultado es una impagable historia particular de Argentina. Y el autorre­trato de un autor gigantesco. El Jarama, de Rafael Sánchez Ferlosio Su autor le cogió manía al libro que lo consagró, pero ni eso ha conseguido borrar las virtudes de esta estupenda novela de agua dulce. ¿Ventajas? El rebote de Ferlosio lo convirtió en el gran ensayista español del último medio siglo. ¿Contraindicaciones? Imposibles de detallar sin destriparlo.

World.title: ‘El viajero’, Éric Cantona resolverá los asesinatos irresueltos
World.content:
El exfutbolista interpreta a un detective privado que cumple escrupulosamente todos los requisitos de la ficción literaria o cinematográfica: solitario, sin dinero, intuitivo y con métodos poco o nada convencionales

Artículos estrictamente de opinión que responden al estilo propio del autor. Estos textos de opinión han de basarse en datos verificados y ser respetuosos con las personas aunque se critiquen sus actos. Todas las columnas de opinión de personas ajenas a la Redacción de EL PAÍS llevarán, tras la última línea, un pie de autor —por conocido que éste sea— donde se indique el cargo, título, militancia política (en su caso) u ocupación principal, o la que esté o estuvo relacionada con el tema abordado

Hay momentos y situaciones en la vida que, por su excepcionalidad, quedan anclados en la mente de los ciudadanos como únicos referentes de una larga trayectoria vital. En enero de 1995, la estrella del Manchester United Éric Cantona fue expulsado de un partido por una dura entrada a un rival. Mientras se retiraba al vestuario, un forofo del Crystal Palace bajó 11 filas de la tribuna para gritarle insultos racistas. Cantona no lo dudó y de un gran salto con las piernas por delante le propinó una gran patada al estilo kung-fu. Esa fue la imagen que quedó de su larga y exitosa carrera futbolística.

Años después, tras “colgar las botas”, que diría un clásico, Éric Cantona se ha convertido en un excelente actor de cine y televisión con papeles mayoritariamente de hombre duro, policía o mafioso indistintamente, según lo exija el guion. Y así aparece como protagonista absoluto en los primeros capítulos de la serie francesa El viajero, en la que, en el papel de un exinspector de la brigada criminal, se dedica a recorrer Francia con su casa-furgoneta para tratar de solucionar alguno de los más de 300 casos de asesinatos sin resolver que se producen anualmente en su país. Un detective privado que cumple escrupulosamente todos los requisitos de la ficción literaria o cinematográfica: solitario, sin dinero, intuitivo y con métodos poco o nada convencionales.

La serie francesa dirigida por Stéphanie Murat que exhibe el canal Cosmo ratifica el profesionalismo y la afición de su industria por los relatos policíacos, una cualidad que ya manifestó André Breton elogiando las novelas de Dashiell Hammett, autor pionero de la “novela negra” tras la publicación de Cosecha roja en 1929.

El viajero cambia de protagonista tras sus primeros cinco capítulos. Éric Cantona deja paso a Bruno Debrandt que, al igual que su predecesor, continuará resolviendo casos criminales irresueltos a lo largo y ancho de la Francia rural, lo que a su vez permite a la productora trabajar en distintas regiones administrativas y gozar de interesantes ventajas y subvenciones. La industria audiovisual, como tantas otras, necesita ayudas suplementarias para su supervivencia y si para conseguirlas conviene rodar en distintos departamentos, pues se rueda. Es una decisión que comparte otra de las series más notables del género, Asesinato en…, realizada en diversas regiones francesas, aunque en este caso los protagonistas cambian en cada capítulo.

World.title: María Consuelo Araújo, la embajadora con la que De la Espriella busca apuntalar la alianza con Estados Unidos
World.content:
La diplomática aterriza en la embajada en Washington, la de mayor interés para el presidente colombiano y a través de la cual quiere impulsar su relación con Trump

El presidente Abelardo de la Espriella anunció este lunes que María Consuelo Araújo será la nueva embajadora de Colombia en Estados Unidos. La excanciller y exministra de Cultura aterriza en una de las delegaciones diplomáticas más importantes para el país en un momento en el que el mandatario colombiano ha mostrado una afinidad total con Donald Trump. Su principal tarea será la de relanzar las relaciones bilaterales con el principal socio comercial del país, pero, a la vez, tendrá que sortear varios retos en materia comercial y de seguridad, grandes prioridades para la Casa Blanca.

“Desde la Embajada de Estados Unidos en Colombia me notifican en este momento que ha llegado el beneplácito para la persona que nominé como embajadora de Colombia en los Estados Unidos. Me complace informarle al país que mi buena amiga, una persona de toda mi confianza y de mis afectos desde hace muchos años, será la nueva embajadora”. Así comunicó De la Espriella el nombramiento de Araújo, conocida en los círculos políticos colombianos por su apodo Conchi, como la máxima representante del país en Washington.

Nacida en Valledupar, Araújo es profesional en Finanzas y Relaciones Internacionales de la Universidad Externado de Colombia. Miembro de una tradicional y poderosa familia del departamento del Cesar, fue nombrada ministra de Cultura durante el Gobierno del presidente Álvaro Uribe con solo 30 años. Después la hizo canciller, aunque solo permaneció seis meses en el cargo. Renunció en febrero de 2006, días después de que su hermano, el exsenador Álvaro Araújo Castro, fuera arrestado por tener vínculos con los paramilitares de las Autodefensas Unidas de Colombia. El excongresista acabó condenado por la Corte Suprema a nueve años de prisión.

La nueva embajadora también cuenta con una carrera en el sector privado, como directora de la minera Gran Colombia Gold y, desde febrero pasado, presidenta ejecutiva de la Cámara Colombiana de la Infraestructura, el gremio de los grandes constructores. También hizo carrera en el Distrito de Bogotá, de la mano del alcalde Enrique Peñalosa, de quien fue directora del Jardín Botánico, secretaria de Integración Social y gerente de TransMilenio, el sistema de transporte masivo de la capital colombiana.

De la Espriella le ha dado a Araújo su visto bueno para reconducir las relaciones con Washington desde, según él, “la embajada más importante” para Colombia. “Me siento honrado y feliz de contar con una mujer de su experiencia, trayectoria, honestidad e inteligencia”, ha loado el mandatario a la política costeña. El presidente ha mostrado una alineación total con Trump y su política exterior.

“Su prioridad debe ser consolidar las relaciones con Estados Unidos, que Gustavo Petro fragmentó de manera profunda. Los enfrentamientos diplomáticos, que acabaron en retirarle la visa e incluirlo en la lista de la OFAC empobreció de una manera insólita un vínculo histórico. Entonces, la tarea primordial de Araújo es que las relaciones vuelvan, al menos, a ser las mismas que antes del Gobierno de Petro”, considera Fabián Cárdenas, catedrático de la Universidad Javeriana y experto en derecho internacional.

Cooperación en seguridad y comercio

Una de las primeras misiones concretas de la nueva embajadora será la de incorporar a Colombia en el llamado Escudo de las Américas, una coalición creada por el republicano que ya integra una veintena de países que comparten métodos para luchar contra las redes del narcotráfico en la región.

A su vez, se espera que renegocie los aranceles impuestos contra Colombia, después de que De la Espriella le pidiera a su homólogo estadounidense un alivio “temporal” sobre estas tasas mientras avanza la recuperación por un terremoto que ya deja casi 300 muertos y cuya crisis costará unos 30 billones de pesos (9,5 millones de dólares), según ha estimado el Gobierno. El presidente anunció este martes que enviará a su ministro de Comercio a Washington para este encargo.

Araújo sucede a Daniel García-Peña, embajador en Washington desde 2024 hasta el final del mandato de Petro. El exdiplomático tuvo que sortear varias crisis generadas por los choques del expresidente izquierdista con la Casa Blanca, como las amenazas de unas tarifas de hasta el 25% y de una posible intervención militar en Bogotá, similar a la de Caracas en enero que acabó con el arresto de Nicolás Maduro. Aunque Petro y Trump limaron sus asperezas a inicios de año con una reunión bilateral en la Casa Blanca, nunca llegaron a simpatizar del todo.

La dinámica ha dado un giro de 180 grados con De la Espriella. Trump lo apoyó cuando aún era candidato y ya ha conversado en al menos dos ocasiones con él. Su Administración también ha tenido contactos con los miembros del nuevo Gobierno en aras de un objetivo común: que Colombia vuelva a ser el socio más confiable de EE UU en Sudamérica. Y ya se han dado pasos agigantados en esa dirección. La semana pasada, Pete Hegseth, secretario de Defensa, anunció que el Gobierno de De la Espriella le autorizó a realizar “operaciones militares conjuntas” para destruir redes del narco en suelo colombiano. El ministro de Defensa, Jorge Eduardo Mora, no ha explicado en qué consistirá esta alianza militar con Washington.

Mientras, Washington también avanza en el nombramiento de un embajador en Bogotá, el primero en más de cuatro años. Durante la presidencia de Petro, la Casa Blanca mantuvo el puesto vacante. Francisco Palmieri fungió como embajador encargado, mientras que John McNamara se mantuvo como encargado de negocios de la delegación hasta su salida en febrero. Trump designó en junio al empresario Nate Morris como nuevo embajador en Colombia, pero el nombramiento aún debe ser ratificado por el Senado antes de que sea oficial.

La medida del éxito de Araújo, según el docente Cárdenas, es “su capacidad de abrir una revisión del tratado de libre comercio para que sea más favorable para los empresarios colombianos”. Además, deberá equilibrar las buenas relaciones con Trump y su Administración sin perderlas del todo con los demócratas, que tienen la posibilidad de recuperar el control del Congreso en las próximas elecciones de medio término. “Por eso es que su labor no es solo la de una embajadora, sino casi la de una gerente de Colombia en Estados Unidos”, resume el experto.

World.title: Number of non-EU dentists in NL doubles in five years
World.content:
The number of dentists trained outside the EU who are moving to the Netherlands to help fill a chronic national shortage has more than doubled in five years, with recent arrivals coming from countries including Syria, South Africa, Turkey, Brazil and Iraq.

One in four dentists now working in the country qualified abroad, according to the dentists’ association KNMT, and in Zeeland more than half were trained overseas.

Figures from the Amsterdam dental school ACTA, which runs the admissions process for applicants from outside the EU, show 120 people are sitting its professional competence test this year, compared with 53 in 2021, the current affairs programme Nieuwsuur reported.

In total, 2,287 dentists with a foreign diploma are working in the Netherlands, a number rising by 150 to 200 a year.

Lack of national funding

The reliance on overseas recruits is partly due to a lack of education funding for Dutch students. Thousands apply but places are very limited. Etienne Verheijck, education director for the ACTA, called that “a policy choice by the education ministry.”

KNMT chair Hans de Vries called it “painful” that motivated young people are rejected by a lottery system, sometimes three times in a row, while the gap is filled from abroad.

The shortage is expected to grow, and the government’s own capacity advisory body has for years urged ministers to open more training places.

Checking your dentist is registered

To work in the Netherlands, dentists with a non-EU diploma must pass a competence test and learn Dutch before they can join the official BIG register of healthcare professionals. Those with an EU diploma need only meet the language requirement.

The healthcare inspectorate IGJ said it regularly receives reports of people performing treatments such as root canals without being registered. De Vries said dentists may work under a registered colleague’s supervision while they qualify, but treating patients unsupervised is improper and potentially unlawful.

Patients can check whether their own dentist appears on the BIG register, which is public and free to search. Dental care in the Netherlands works differently from many other countries, and full practices unable to take on new patients are already a common complaint.

A 12-year-old Dutch boy is being treated in intensive care after falling 30 metres (100ft) while walking in the Austrian alps.

Local media reported that the boy was walking with his father when he slipped and fell while crossing rocky terrain in the Tirol mountain range at 11am on Tuesday.

The pair were descending the Gänsekragen mountain after reaching the 2,914m (9,560ft) summit at 9.30am.

They were walking along a waymarked path towards a mountain hut in Winnebachsee when the accident happened about 500m below the summit as the boy rounded a corner.

The 46-year-old man managed to climb down the hillside to his son, who was lying unconscious, and raise the alarm. An air ambulance transported him to a clinic in Innsbruck, where he is being treated for serious injuries.

Police are investigating how the boy fell.

World.title: Schiphol security staff begin strike action over workload
World.content:
Security staff at Schiphol will begin short work stoppages and deliberately slow-downs in the coming days, after the airport and its three security firms missed a union deadline to ease a workload the unions say has become unmanageable. Travellers could face longer queues as a result.

Unions FNV and CNV announced the action on Wednesday, after an ultimatum to Schiphol and the firms Securitas, I-SEC and Trigion expired at midday. The stoppages will be flagged only a few hours in advance, and the unions have not ruled out longer strikes if nothing changes.

“Nobody wants industrial action at Schiphol,” said CNV negotiator André Quist. “But if employers take no concrete step against the enormous workload even after a crystal-clear ultimatum, they leave our members no choice.”

The dispute dates back to a shake-up in the spring, when Schiphol cut the number of firms running hand-baggage checks from five to three. The switch to new employers affected most of the airport’s roughly 5,000 security guards, whose pay was preserved but whose rosters, shift times, breaks and leave all changed.

Since then, the unions say, workloads have risen and sickness absence has climbed, leaving fewer guards to carry the same load – a downward spiral they warn is getting worse.

In July the unions made eight demands, including longer breaks, two consecutive days off after five worked, a heat protocol for the terminals, and at least two women on every security lane so female passengers can be searched. A lane should close, they say, if only one woman is available.

Schiphol said it regretted the action and took the guards’ concerns seriously, adding that it and the three firms were already working on improvements to five of the eight demands. It said it would do all it could to limit the impact on travellers.

A separate walkout by around 350 cleaners at the airport also happened on Wednesday for two hours around midday in a dispute over reduced sick pay in the national cleaning agreement, which FNV wants Schiphol, as a major client, to help resist.

Ajax fans who want to watch the club’s crucial Conference League play-off match against Swiss club Sion will have to pay €4.99 after the broadcasting rights were acquired by Talpa.

The match, which kicks off at 8.15pm on Thursday, is being shown on Talpa’s pay-per-view channel KIJK, angering many Dutch fans.

The decision also went down badly with Ziggo, Ajax’s main sponsor and one of the Netherlands’ biggest commercial sports broadcasters.

Ziggo has the exclusive rights to show matches in UEFA’s main competitions, but qualifying rounds are not covered by that deal.

The company posted a message on social media site X, formerly Twitter, explaining that Sion as the home club was entitled to sell the broadcasting rights to the highest bidder.

The return leg in Amsterdam next Thursday, August 27, will be screen on Ziggo’s free subscription channel.

On Wednesday, NEC Nijmegen will be hoping to take a step towards the Champions League group stages as they host Norwegian side Bodø/Glimt in the first leg of their play-off tie. The match is being shown on Ziggo Sport, with the return leg in Norway next Tuesday, August 25.

Criminal gangs are earning millions by importing canned drinks to bypass the Dutch deposit return system.

The black market has sprung up since a compulsory 15 cent deposit was imposed on all drinks cans in 2023, as part of the Dutch government’s plans to cut waste.

The environmental standards inspectorate ILT estimates that up to 50 million illegally imported bottles are sold every year, often in restaurants and cafés that buy them from illegal traders.

In an echo of the Netherlands’ cannabis policy, importing canned drinks is outlawed, but buying and selling them after they cross the border is not, making the drinks attractive to outlets that want to avoid the cost and logistical burden of recycling thousands of cans.

Soft drinks are bought from Germany and Denmark, while beer is more commonly imported from Poland, all countries in the border-free Schengen zone.

The result is that the cans end up in landfill or as litter, hampering the government’s efforts to meet its recycling targets.

“It’s an illegal trade,” ILT acting inspector-general Edwin van Houten told EenVandaag. “They come into contact with organised crime because there is a huge amount of money to be earned from avoiding the rules. It runs into the millions of euros.”

Van Houten said the rules were difficult to enforce because only importation is illegal. In the last year 500 inspections were carried out and 90 companies were given warnings, but only five were fined.

“It’s a drop in the ocean and it costs a lot of capacity because we need to do far-reaching, deep investigations,” he said.

World.title: Parents of euthanasia teen go to court over prosecution letter
World.content:
The parents of a 17-year-old girl who chose to die by euthanasia in 2023 due to incurable psychological suffering have gone to court to force public prosecutors to identify a group of doctors that wrote a damning letter about the case.

Their daughter Milou’s psychological struggles were documented in a 2023 documentary, which covered her wish to be granted the right to voluntary death and the aftermath that followed.

The case caused significant public controversy and a group of 14 doctors subsequently wrote a letter suggesting a criminal investigation should be launched against the parents and doctors involved in treating her.

They called on prosecutors to find out “to what extent those close to this vulnerable patient (…) influenced this young patient’s decision to choose euthanasia.” The writers of the letter did not know Milou or her personal background and had not spoken to her themselves.

Eight of the signatories of the letter are still unnamed. In a courtroom in The Hague on Tuesday, the mother of Milou recounted how that letter had led to daily threats and intimidation, requiring the police to guard their home.

“As a parent, losing your child and having to miss them forever is the worst thing that can happen to you,” the mother Mireille Verhoof told the court. “Being accused afterwards of inciting the death of your child or being complicit in her death is beyond description and unbearable.”

She also said her daughter had effectively been “abused” by anti-euthanasia campaigners, who dismissed their integrity to further a political agenda.

The family’s lawyer Richard Korver also said that the people behind the letter should not be able to use their professional authority to make serious accusations and at the same time claim anonymity, reported to Omroep Brabant.

The public prosecution department still does not want to release the names so as to avoid further conflict and ensure people can bring judicial complaints in confidence. It also disputes that the letter was meant as a formal request for criminal proceedings.

The federation of doctors KNMG also condemned the letter, describing it as “indecent and unacceptable.” The court’s decision on the release of the names is expected on September 3.

If you or someone close to you is struggling with thoughts of suicide, help is available. In the Netherlands, call 113 or 0800-0113 (free) for 24/7 support, or visit 113.nl, where the chat service is available in English.

World.title: Dutch shops to stock more GM food after EU relaxes rules in 2028
World.content:
More genetically modified food is likely to appear in Dutch stores when rules on licensing and labelling are relaxed in two years’ time.

The European parliament passed a law before the summer recess allowing food retailers to stock products containing GM ingredients without labelling them as such, as long as they account for less than 1% of the contents.

The more flexible law was brought in to offset the effect of stricter limits on pesticides, which the EU wanted to halve by 2030, so that growers could use genetic modification to make their crops more resistant to parasites.

But two years ago the EU dropped the pesticides bill, which commission president Ursula von der Leyen said had become “a symbol of polarisation”, while still going ahead with the relaxation of GM rules.

Food products that have been significantly changed by genetic modification will still have to be licensed and labelled under the current rules.

Michelle Habets, a researcher at the Rathenau Institute, a science and technology think tank based in The Hague, said the more flexible rules risked undermining public confidence in supermarkets and other food retailers.

She told NOS she had spoken to dozens of consumers about the new law while it was passing through the European parliament. “Everyone agreed that genetically modified crops should be labelled,” she said.

“People admitted they don’t always study every label in the supermarket, but they think transparency is important, as is the freedom of choice for people who don’t want to eat those crops for whatever reason.”

Jeroen Candel, associate professor of food and agricultural policy at Wageningen University, said GM crops could bring benefits by reducing the need for pesticides, but added a note of caution.

“The new law is based on the idead that we can optimalise the current system of agriculture with new technology,” he said. “But if we do that, we are maintaining a system that is not sustainable in terms of climate and biodiversity.”

World.title: Dutch media attack “chilling” fines for slimming drugs coverage
World.content:
Dutch media companies have been hit with fines running into the tens of millions of euros after inspectors ruled that their reporting on weight loss drugs such as Ozempic amounted to advertising.

Editors described the penalties, issued by the health department’s inspectorate IGJ, as “bizarre” and an attack on press freedom.

The verdicts covered newspapers across the range and political spectrum of Dutch media including NRC, the Volkskrant, the Telegraaf and AD.

The inspectors said the coverage of medicines such as Ozempic, Wegovy and Mounjaro was too positive because it reported that the benefits of the drugs went beyond treating diabetes, the only condition they are prescribed for in the Netherlands.

The Dutch Medicines Act bans advertising for prescription medicines. The IGJ said it had issued around 20 fines between 2023 for breaching the law, not just to media companies.

Science reporting

The inspectorate would not go into individual cases, but DPG Media, one of the two main news publishers in the Netherlands, said it had been fined €48,500 in April for two articles in local newspaper De Stentor and lifestyle magazine Flair, and another €51,000 this month for articles in the Volkskrant and AD.

Mediahuis was fined a total of €132,000 this month for articles in NRC’s science section and the Telegraaf.

The IGJ said: “We weigh up the facts carefully in each case, including the interests of patients. In the case of media coverage we look at the whole picture: content, context, images and audio. It’s not a tick list.”

The journalists’ union NVJ said it was “shocked” that the inspectorate had imposed fines on reporters “who regularly write about medicines and have no other interest than informing the public.”

General secretary Thomas Bruning called for talks with the health ministry to discuss the sanctions. “This makes it impossible for journalists to report on this subject in a normal fashion,” he said. “We are taking it very seriously.”

Press freedom

Pieter Klok, editor of the Volkskrant, said he respected the ban on advertising and the IGJ’s right to enforce it. “But I don’t think it should be applied to journalism, unless you can show it’s been paid for,” he said.

Telegraaf editor Kamran Ullah said it would have a “huge chilling effect” on journalists reporting on health issues.

“That goes not just for large news organisations like us, but maybe even more for smaller titles and freelancers. Big publishers can pay these fines, but a fine of more than €100,000 is the equivalent of two journalists’ annual salary.

“That’s a real infringement of press freedom, because if we have to pay these fines, we can’t employ as many journalists.”

We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has unveiled plans to reduce income tax rates for an estimated 3.5 million people earning around or slightly above average salaries. The costs of the cuts would be covered by increasing the tax rate for large companies and individuals with the highest earnings. The changes, which Prime Minister Donald Tusk says are intended to “provide relief and assistance to the growing middle class”, would come into effect from next year – when the government is facing re-election. However, the proposals still require approval from parliament, where Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, has a majority, and President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition and has vetoed a record number of bills. 📊 Nowa skala PIT będzie lepiej dopasowana do rosnących wynagrodzeń. Do 130 tys. zł pozostaje stawka 12%, między 130 a 150 tys. zł pojawi się 24%, a 32% zacznie obowiązywać dopiero powyżej 150 tys. zł. 💰 #WięcejWPortfelu pic.twitter.com/1S2MpSkVoC — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 19, 2026 The main elements of the proposed changes, which were outlined by Tusk and finance minister Andrzej Domański on Wednesday, are an increase in the earnings threshold at which the lowest rate of income tax is paid and the introduction of a new rate between the lowest and highest earnings brackets. Currently, there are two income tax brackets: the first taxes earnings of up to 120,000 zloty (around €27,800) at a rate of 12%; the second taxes earnings above that level at a rate of 32%. There is also a tax-free allowance for earnings of up to 30,000 zloty. Meanwhile, anyone who earns more than 1 million zloty a year pays an additional “solidarity levy” (effectively a third tax bracket) of 4% on income above that amount. Under the new proposals, the threshold for the first 12% tax bracket would be raised to 130,000 zloty. For earnings between 130,000 and 150,000 zloty, a new tax bracket of 24% would be introduced. Then earnings above 150,000 would be taxed at 32%. Tusk noted that, since his government took office, wages in Poland have increased by around 30%, bringing increasing numbers of people into the higher tax bracket. According to figures from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, in June this year, average monthly earnings at companies employing more than nine people were 9,401.58 zloty, the equivalent of almost 113,000 zloty a year. “We’re not talking about millionaires here; we’re talking about a growing middle class…on whose shoulders the financing of state security, defence spending, etc. rests to a large extent,” said Domański. “We want to change this…so that those who work hard to earn their average wage can clearly feel the relief,” added Tusk. “And we want this to be financed by the wealthiest companies and the wealthiest individuals, who have the lowest tax burden.” The number of ultra-wealthy individuals in Poland has more than doubled since 2021, a faster rate of growth than anywhere else in the world, according to a new study https://t.co/MNKgmjzn2U — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 11, 2026 Therefore, in order to finance the middle-class tax cuts, Tusk and Domański announced that the government would seek to increase corporate income tax from 19% to 22% for firms and tax capital groups that generate annual revenues above €50 million. Meanwhile, the solidarity levy for individuals earning over 1 million zloty a year would be increased by one percentage point, to 5%. “I am absolutely convinced that this will make our tax system more equitable,” declared Tusk. However, he also conceded that raising the income-tax-free amount from 30,000 to 60,000 zloty – as his Civic Platform (KO) party promised to do within its first 100 days in office – would not be possible for budgetary reasons, in particular the need to finance high defence spending. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) tax free. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build savings and channel money into the domestic financial market https://t.co/1xDHHJGYKX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 14, 2026 The prime minister said that the planned tax changes would be discussed further this week at a cabinet meeting devoted to next year’s state budget, which is currently being prepared. The relevant legislation will subsequently be submitted to parliament, with the aim of bringing it into force in 2027. However, Tusk acknowledged that there is a strong possibility of a veto by Nawrocki, who has blocked dozens of government bills, including fiscal measures. In December, Nawrocki vetoed an increase in the tax on alcoholic and sweet drinks. Last month, he effectively blocked a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits by sending it to the constitutional court for review. However, he did approve a law increasing the corporate income tax rate for banks. President @NawrockiKn has obstructed a planned windfall tax on fuel companies by sending it to the constitutional court, where it could stay for years The tax aimed to offset fuel price protection costs after the Iran war surgehttps://t.co/UojVuYhvdV — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 Next year’s budget will be closely watched given that Poland’s fiscal situation has become increasingly problematic in recent years. In 2024, the European Union placed Poland under its excessive deficit procedure, requiring Warsaw to commit to measures to bring down the deficit. However, last year the deficit actually rose, from 6.4% of GDP in 2024 to 7.3% in 2025, which was the second-highest level among all EU member states. This year, Poland’s public debt passed the EU’s limit of 60% of GDP for the first time on record. The situation has led two of the big three rating agencies, Fitch and Moody’s, to shift Poland’s credit outlook to negative. This year, Fitch warned that the political gridlock between Nawrocki and the government was making tackling the deficit and debt more difficult. Given that Poland will hold parliamentary elections in autumn 2027, it is unlikely that either the government or Nawrocki – who will be supporting the right-wing opposition – will be keen on any fiscal measures that either raise taxes or reduce spending in areas such as social policy and defence. Poland’s public debt has passed 60% of GDP for the first time, thereby exceeding the limit enshrined in EU law. The country is already under the EU's excessive deficit procedure, requiring it to take steps to bring public finances under greater control https://t.co/LNJ0YrP2Ge — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 12, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland launches tourism campaign featuring Lewandowski, Eisenberg and Rubik
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has launched a new advertising campaign to promote itself internationally and attract more tourists from “key European markets” and the United States. The new initiative, which has the slogan “Poland. More than you expected”, features global Polish icons such as football star Robert Lewandowski, supermodel Anja Rubik, and Hollywood filmmaker Jesse Eisenberg, who received Polish citizenship last year. A series of videos, the first of which was released Tuesday, will aim to present Poland as “modern, safe, diverse and authentic”, as well as “defying stereotypes”, says sports and tourism minister Jakub Rutnicki. Commissioned by his ministry and launched by the Polish Tourism Organisation (POT), the campaign will be conducted in Germany, Spain, Italy, the United Kingdom and the United States. The first video promotes Warsaw, Poland’s capital, and features Lewandowski, Rubik and Eisenberg appearing near the city’s landmarks. Polish actor Nikodem Rozbicki, meanwhile, plays the role of renowned 19th-century Polish composer Fryderyk Chopin. In the 30-second spot, Chopin’s character declares that Warsaw is “where my heart is” – a reference to the fact that Chopin’s heart, preserved in cognac, was brought back to the city from Paris by his sister shortly after his death in 1849 and is now immured in a pillar in the city’s Holy Cross Church. Lewandowski, who recently joined US football team Chicago Fire, tells viewers that Poland offers “more than you expected”, a reference to the campaign’s main slogan, which suggests to viewers that Poland may surprise them positively. “Research shows that people who have visited Poland rate it much more favourably than their previous perceptions or media reports suggested,” notes POT in its press release. Magdalena Krucz, the head of POT, adds that she believes the campaign “will be as surprising to audiences as Poland itself is to tourists who come to us for the first time”. However, the slogan is not new: it has been used by POT to promote Poland since 2021. The new campaign will also feature Nobel Peace Prize winner and former president Lech Wałęsa, who led the Solidarity movement that brought down Poland’s former communist regime. POT notes that he remains “one of the most recognisable symbols in the world of the fight for freedom and democracy”. The music is arranged by Radzimir Dębski, better known as Jimek, a Polish composer and conductor who has regularly performed with US rap legend Snoop Dogg. Polish-American NBA star @JeremySochan has joined a campaign to promote Poland as a tourist destination. His appearance has been received positively, but Sochan responded directly to one commentator who said a black person shouldn't be advertising Poland https://t.co/KXDok7IAXP — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 15, 2024 Poland has experienced a tourism boom in recent years. Last year, the country recorded the European Union’s second-fastest growth in the number of nights spent in tourist accommodation, behind only Malta. The biggest tourist draw is the historic city of Kraków, which was last year named the best city break destination in Europe by members of British consumer association and magazine Which? for the fifth time. This year, Time Out magazine rated Kraków the 16th best city in the world. However, the country has a wide range of tourist-friendly destinations, including long, sandy beaches on the northern Baltic coast, mountains in the south, the lake district of Masuria, as well as many historic cities and modern museums and galleries. Poland saw the EU's second-fastest growth in tourism in 2025, behind only the Mediterranean island state of Malta https://t.co/WVkRbHtU7o — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 19, 2026 The city of Lublin in eastern Poland, which will be a European City of Culture in 2029, last year welcomed a record 2.2 million visitors, including over half a million from abroad. The city is known for its rich Jewish history, and featured prominently in the 2024 Oscar-nominated film A Real Pain, directed by and starring Eisenberg, whose ancestors were Jews from Lublin and the nearby town of Krasnystaw. Last year, the sport and tourism ministry announced that it wants tourism to contribute 9% of GDP within a decade, from about 5% now. The strategy includes creating a “Polish brand” through which internationally recognised athletes, artists, historical figures and products are showcased more prominently. Last month, the government appointed a marketing and branding expert to develop a unified strategy for promoting the country abroad, saying the move will help boost tourism, support Polish products and attract foreign investment. The city of Lublin in eastern Poland welcomed a record 2.2 million visitors in 2025. That included 506,000 from abroad, which was also the highest ever figure, with Brits, Israelis and Americans the most common foreign visitors https://t.co/6yMrRcf6ml — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 28, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Warsaw Uprising veteran and activist Wanda Traczyk-Stawska dies aged 99
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Wanda Traczyk-Stawska, a veteran of the Warsaw Uprising against Nazi-German occupation during World War Two, has died aged 99. Traczyk-Stawska, who survived imprisonment in German camps after the uprising, in her later years became a vocal advocate for the rights of women and disabled people. “Warsaw has lost someone extraordinary,” wrote Warsaw’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, announcing her death on Wednesday. “A heroine, a soldier…but above all a teacher who, throughout her life, taught us what matters most: courage, dignity, and responsibility for our fellow human beings.” Odeszła Pani Wanda. Trudno w to uwierzyć. Warszawa straciła kogoś wyjątkowego – Bohaterkę, żołnierkę Powstania Warszawskiego, Honorową Obywatelkę miasta. Ale przede wszystkim nauczycielkę, która przez całe życie uczyła nas tego, co najważniejsze: odwagi, godności i… pic.twitter.com/uSNcsZ7c1P — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) August 19, 2026 Traczyk-Stawska, born in Warsaw in 1927, was only 12 years old when Nazi Germany invaded Poland. She initially became involved in the Grey Ranks (Szare Szeregi), an underground resistance movement associated with the Polish scouting movement, participating in sabotage operations. She later joined the Home Army (AK), Poland’s main resistance force, and, at the age of 17, served as a riflewoman and liaison during the Warsaw Uprising, taking the nom de guerre “Pączek” (meaning “Bud”). Traczyk-Stawska was seriously injured while fighting in the uprising. After the revolt was defeated, she was taken prisoner and subsequently held in various prisoner-of-war camps in Germany until the end of the war. After returning to Poland, Traczyk-Stawska earned a degree in psychology and began working as a teacher of disabled children in Warsaw. At the same time, she became an active figure in commemorating the uprising and its participants. In her final years, Traczyk-Stawska also became politically active. In 2018, she visited parliament to support a protest by disabled people and their carers, who were seeking more state support. Two years later, at the age of 93, she and another female uprising veteran, Hanna Stadnik, joined the mass Women’s Strike protests that broke out in response to the introduction of a near-total ban on abortion under the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. “We women will not relent this time,” she told broadcaster TVN at the time. “In the uprising, we fought for our freedom, because there is no dignity without freedom. If we are currently treated like incubators, we have the right to fight for our dignity…We will fight – unarmed, but to the last woman – not to be treated like objects.” Traczyk-Stawska was also among a group of female Uprising veterans who that year criticised PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński for wearing, during a speech condemning the Women’s Strike protests, a badge featuring the anchor symbol that was used by the Home Army during the war. She was also an advocate for women’s rights more broadly. In 2023, in a speech at the 79th anniversary of the uprising, Traczyk-Stawska noted that, “at the beginning, the generals shouted: ‘Why do we need so many women?'” But, by the time the uprising ended, “we had been given the same rights as boys. And we won’t get rid of these rights. Because everyone, whether a man or a woman, is a citizen of this country and has equality written into the constitution”. Her speech then became overtly political, saying that “this [PiS] government needs to be completely changed, as it doesn’t remember that women have their own position enshrined in the constitution. That we are equal to men.” In both the 2020 and 2025 presidential elections, Traczyk-Stawska expressed support for the candidacy of Trzaskowski, who is a deputy leader of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party that is PiS’s main opponent. However, in both elections, Trzaskowski lost to PiS-backed candidates. Odeszła Wanda Traczyk-Stawska ps. „Pączek” – Bohaterka, Patriotka, wzór odwagi i niezłomności. Pokazywała, że prawdziwy patriotyzm to budowanie wspólnoty, empatia i otwartość na świat. Cześć Jej pamięci! 🕯️🤍 Najgłębsze wyrazy współczucia dla Bliskich. pic.twitter.com/nY0ijDSBlJ — Monika Sikora ⚡️ (@Moni_Sikora) August 19, 2026 Following news of Traczyk-Stawska’s death, many prominent figures paid tribute to her, in particular from the current KO-led ruling coalition. “Farewell, heroine,” wrote KO leader and Prime Minister Donald Tusk, sharing a photo of himself with Traczyk-Stawska and quoting one of her statements: “Do not stand, do not watch when evil happens, but react immediately, for that is your duty.” While she had fought against German occupation, Traczyk-Stawska later called for reconciliation. In her 2023 speech, she called Germany “our best neighbour” and said that the two countries must now “stand together”, including supporting Ukraine against Russian aggression. Today, Germany’s ambassador to Poland, Miguel Berger, expressed his “great sadness” at Traczyk-Stawska’s death, calling her an “advocate of dialogue in the process of Polish-German reconciliation and a passionate champion of peace, freedom, and human dignity”. „Nie stój, nie patrz, gdy się zło dzieje, tylko reaguj natychmiast, bo to jest twój obowiązek." – Wanda Traczyk-Stawska Żegnaj, Bohaterko. pic.twitter.com/MhfqlszVcI — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) August 19, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland “99% sure” fugitive opposition politician is in pro-Russian breakaway region of Moldova
